findings.title: Process-spawning tests (restore-check, backup-cli) run under the default 5 s timeout while their siblings get 30 s; the pdf.js test races its 15 s; the gate goes red on a loaded machine
findings.evidence: Seven tests in tests/unit/restore-check.test.ts spawn `node scripts/restore-check.mjs` with no per-test timeout (line 51, line 60 which spawns twice, and the five cases of the it.each at 67-78), and five in tests/unit/backup-cli.test.ts spawn scripts/backup.mjs the same way (line 45 and the four cases of the it.each at 51-62). vitest.config.ts sets no testTimeout, so each has 5000 ms, while the two scrypt tests in restore-check.test.ts pass 30_000. restore-check.mjs statically imports @supabase/supabase-js (line 31) before it parses argv (lines 48-58), so even --help pays that import. Measured on the owner's machine, idle: `node scripts/restore-check.mjs --help` took 1748-2511 ms, `node scripts/backup.mjs --help` 775-2002 ms, bare `node -e 0` 1119-1392 ms. In the baseline (artifacts/acceptance/FABLE-AUDIT/before/test.log), five restore-check tests failed with 'Test timed out in 5000ms' at 5742-9293 ms, and reader-mapping.test.ts:169 failed at 27442 ms against its 15_000 (idle here, the pdf.js import takes 1055-5168 ms and the parse 1414-2062 ms; fixLigatures is linear and is not the cause).
findings.impact: pnpm test, and pnpm check, which is the acceptance gate, fail on the owner's machine whenever it is loaded, for reasons unrelated to the code. A suite that is known to be red for no reason teaches the orchestrator to discount real failures. CI runs on an unloaded Linux runner and stays green, so the flake is only seen locally.
findings.proposed_fix: Give every spawn test the same explicit timeout as its siblings (e.g. `{ timeout: 30_000 }` on the restore-check describes at lines 50 and 59 and on backup-cli's describe at line 44), and give the pdf.js test 60_000. Optionally, move the supabase-js import in restore-check.mjs below the argument parsing (as a dynamic import) so --help and usage errors never load it.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:TEST-UNIT-01 and lead:TEST-UNIT-02. The brief asked whose fault the timeouts are: the tests'. They give a fixed 5 s to a Node process spawn and 15 s to a 2 MB library import plus font parsing on a starved machine. The code adds only the avoidable eager supabase-js import.

findings.title: The stats test that claims 'only the analytics part stays cached' cannot fail: the clock is frozen and analytics is unconfigured
findings.evidence: beforeEach fakes Date at NOW and never advances it (lines 695-700). The test then asserts `expect(second.body.data.generatedAt).toBe(first.body.data.generatedAt)` and that `analytics` is equal (lines 727-728). ownerStats() builds `generatedAt: new Date().toISOString()` (stats.ts:16). With ANALYTICS_TOKEN unset, fetchAnalytics() returns the constant {status:'unavailable', reason:'NOT_CONFIGURED'} (analytics.ts:233). Both values are the same with or without the cache, so deleting the cache check at admin.ts:564 (`if (cachedStats && Date.now() - cachedStats.at < cachedStats.ttl) return ...`) or swapping the 5-minute and 30-second TTLs (admin.ts:570) leaves every unit test green.
findings.impact: The per-isolate analytics cache (5 min for a good answer, 30 s for a failure) has no working test. A regression that disables it sends two Cloudflare GraphQL queries every time the owner views stats (the dashboard and the owner home both read them). A regression that inverts the expiry shows the owner a stale or failed analytics answer indefinitely. The test name tells a reviewer the cache is proven.
findings.proposed_fix: In that test, configure analytics (ANALYTICS_TOKEN, CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID, SITE_URL) with a stubbed fetch that counts calls. Advance the faked clock between the two calls (after 1 minute: no new fetch; after 6 minutes: a second fetch; 31 s after an 'unavailable' answer: a refetch), and assert the fetch count, not generatedAt.

findings.title: '429 (quota / rate limit) is a retry' never sends a quota error, so the QUOTA classification the outbox stops on has no CI test
findings.evidence: The test sends only `{ name: 'rate_limit_exceeded' }` with 429 and expects error 'RATE_LIMIT'. email.ts:62-64 maps `daily_quota_exceeded` and `monthly_quota_exceeded` to error 'QUOTA', and outbox.ts:281 stops the run only on `outcome.error === 'QUOTA'` (the SQL gives the attempt back only for QUOTA). No unit test sends either quota name (grep of tests/unit for daily_quota_exceeded finds none). The only coverage is tests/integration/email-delivery.test.ts:346, and CI runs `pnpm test` only (.github/workflows/ci.yml: 'Not run here ... pnpm test:db'). The names themselves match Resend's current errors page.
findings.impact: A one-line regression in the quota branch (e.g. comparing `error.name` instead of `name`, or a renamed constant) turns every quota refusal into RATE_LIMIT. The outbox then keeps claiming after Resend's daily cap, each row burns an attempt instead of waiting for the UTC reset, and receipts can reach 'exhausted' on a busy day. CI stays green; only a local test:db run would notice.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `daily_quota_exceeded` and `monthly_quota_exceeded` cases (429 -> {outcome:'retry', error:'QUOTA'}) to email.test.ts. Add one outbox.test.ts case where the first send answers 429 daily_quota_exceeded and the run stops after one claim, with outbox_result p_error 'QUOTA'.

findings.title: Nothing pins each form's Turnstile widget action to the action its function expects, and local keys skip the check
findings.evidence: The four widgets each pass a literal: useTurnstile('contact') (ContactForm.tsx:52), useTurnstile('notify') (AvailabilityForm.tsx:83), useTurnstile('checkout') (CheckoutForm.tsx:158) and useTurnstile('order-recover') (OrderPage.tsx:306). The functions compare against separate literals (checkout.ts:433, contact.ts:133, notify.ts:142, orders.ts:190). The unit tests pin only the server side (checkout.test.ts:867, notify.test.ts:246, orders.test.ts:289, contact-route.test.ts:99). Every local run uses the always-pass test secret (scripts/local-env.mjs:49), for which verifyTurnstile returns ok before the action check (turnstile.ts:107-111), so the e2e suite cannot see a mismatch either.
findings.impact: Renaming the action on either side (for example a widget action changed in a UI edit) passes lint, the unit suite and the whole local e2e battery. On the hosted site, every real submission of that form is then refused with 400 «تعذّر التحقق من أنك إنسان.»: no checkout, no contact message, no order-link recovery. The break would surface only at the hosted P11 check or from buyers.
findings.proposed_fix: Export one constant per action from a shared module (e.g. TURNSTILE_ACTIONS = {contact, notify, checkout, recover} in supabase/functions/_shared/turnstile.ts) and use it on both sides. Alternatively, add a unit test that reads the useTurnstile(...) argument of the four components and compares it with the expectedAction each handler passes (the handler tests already capture it).
findings.prior_overlap: AUDIT-1 S20.6 added only the server-side assertions.

findings.title: staff-admin's owner and TOTP gate has no CI test: the unit test mocks it to 'owner, fresh TOTP', and the integration test covers only an editor and an aal1 owner
findings.evidence: `vi.mock('../../supabase/functions/_shared/staff.ts', () => ({ staffFromRequest: async () => ({ userId: ..., role: 'owner', recentTotp: true }) }))` replaces the caller's identity in every case. As a result, staff-admin/index.ts:51 (`if (staff.role !== 'owner') return fail(403, ...)`) and :52 (`if (!staff.recentTotp) return fail(403, 'STEP_UP_REQUIRED', ...)`) never run for a non-owner in the unit suite. The only other coverage, tests/integration/staff-admin.test.ts:17 and :25, calls the function as an editor and as an aal1 owner. No test calls staff-admin as operations, as a revoked member (role null), or as an aal2 owner whose TOTP is older than five minutes, and CI does not run test:db (.github/workflows/ci.yml, closing comment).
findings.impact: These two lines are the only guard on inviting staff, changing roles and revoking members: the SQL cannot see aal/amr, as admin.ts's header also says of its own gates. A one-line regression such as writing the check as a denylist (`if (staff.role === 'editor')`) would let an operations member call set_role on themselves and become owner. Dropping line 52 would let a stolen aal1 owner session invite an attacker. Lint, typecheck, the unit suite and CI would all stay green, and the local integration file would still pass with the denylist. PLANS/VERIFICATION.md lists as non-negotiable: 'Real JWTs for anon/editor/operations/owner/revoked through ... every Edge Function; forbid self-promotion ... and owner-aal2 bypass'.
findings.proposed_fix: Make the identity a per-test value in the unit mock (hoisted, like `hoisted.client`) and add cases: editor, operations and null role -> 403 FORBIDDEN; owner with recentTotp false -> 403 STEP_UP_REQUIRED; null identity -> 401. Each case should assert that no client call (createUser or update) was made. Add operations and revoked callers to tests/integration/staff-admin.test.ts.
findings.prior_overlap: AUDIT-1 X5.15 added operations and revoked callers to staff.test.ts (the Data API), not to the staff-admin function.

findings.title: No test isolates staffFromRequest's `active` check: the only fake staff row is always an active owner
findings.evidence: authReturns() always answers the staff lookup with `{ data: { role: 'owner', active: true }, error: null }`. No unit test feeds `active: false`, an unknown role, a staff lookup error (STAFF_LOOKUP_FAILED) or a header without 'Bearer '. The check at staff.ts:47, `const role = staff.data?.active && ROLES.has(staff.data.role) ? ... : null`, is therefore unpinned. The one integration case with a revoked owner and a live session (tests/integration/disputes-http.test.ts:196-201) goes through dispute-record, whose SQL rechecks the actor, so it answers 403 even without the function's own check. staff-admin.test.ts checks a revoked member only through the Data API (`current_staff_role`) and a new sign-in.
findings.impact: For staff-admin (invite, set_role, set_active: direct service-role table writes), the owner-only `status` and `stats`, and `paid-file-ticket` (a signed upload URL with no SQL call), this line is the only thing that stops a member who was revoked a moment ago but whose access token is still valid (until it expires). Dropping `staff.data?.active &&` in a refactor passes every unit and integration test, and a revoked owner with a fresh TOTP could then restore themselves with set_active. D13 says a revoked member loses access on the next call.
findings.proposed_fix: Add unit cases to service-client-errors.test.ts: `{role:'owner', active:false}` -> role null; `{role:'superuser', active:true}` -> role null; no staff row -> role null; a lookup error -> throws STAFF_LOOKUP_FAILED; 'Basic x' or no header -> null without calling getClaims. Optionally add one integration case: revoke an owner who has a live aal2 session, then call admin `status` and staff-admin and expect 403.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:TEST-UNIT-06 (rated low there; raised because this line is the only guard for staff-admin, status, stats and paid-file-ticket)

findings.title: preorderCurrent compares a date string against the browser's en-CA locale format; its unit test proves only Node's ICU
findings.evidence: `return shipsOn >= new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-CA', { timeZone: 'Asia/Riyadh' }).format(now)` runs in the buyer's browser (a 'use client' component, used at line 151) and assumes en-CA's default date output is 'YYYY-MM-DD'. That is locale data, not a spec guarantee: CLDR 42/ICU 72 changed en-CA to M/d/y, and Chromium and Firefox later patched it back to y-MM-dd (mullvad-browser commit 32434f8e: revert the date format for en-CA per cldr PR 2759). tests/unit/store-availability.test.ts:127-136 runs under Node's bundled ICU, so it passes whatever a buyer's browser does. With '10/4/2026', `'2026-10-03' >= '10/4/2026'` is true ('2' sorts after '1'), so every past date reads as current. The codebase already computes the Riyadh day without locale data: `riyadhToday` (src/lib/admin-money.ts:389) and admin-commerce.ts:56.
findings.impact: On a browser whose ICU carries the M/d/y en-CA data, a static product page built before its preorder date passed keeps showing «طلب مسبق: يُسلَّم في …» with the past date and the preorder button, which is exactly what the guard is meant to stop. The server still decides what can be bought, so the harm is a wrong promise on the page, not a wrong order.
findings.proposed_fix: Compute the Riyadh day without locale data, e.g. `new Date(now.getTime() + 3 * 3_600_000).toISOString().slice(0, 10)`, or reuse riyadhToday from src/lib/admin-money.ts, and keep the existing test. Optionally add one case that stubs Intl.DateTimeFormat to return '10/4/2026', to prove the function no longer depends on it.

findings.title: clientKeyHash: no test would notice the pepper or the daily salt being dropped from the hashed IP
findings.evidence: The only clientKeyHash test hashes two requests with the same pepper ('pepper') at the same moment and compares them (lines 55-57). rate-limit.ts:62 builds `${pepper}:${utcDate}:${throttleAddress(requestIp(request))}`. Deleting `${pepper}:` or `${utcDate}:` from that template leaves every unit test green, since no test varies the pepper or the clock. The hashes are stored as finance.rate_limits.key_hash (20260926120000_contacts_and_email.sql:49) for every throttled endpoint.
findings.impact: Without the pepper, an IPv4 hash can be reversed by hashing all 2^32 addresses, so the promise that a raw IP is never stored (rate-limit.ts:2-6, the privacy data map) silently stops holding for the rate_limits rows and every backup of them. Without the date, a visitor's hash links across days. Neither regression changes any visible behaviour, so only a test can catch it.
findings.proposed_fix: Add two assertions: the same request hashes differently under pepper 'a' and pepper 'b'; and, with vi.useFakeTimers({toFake:['Date']}), the same request hashes differently at 2026-10-05T23:59:59Z and 2026-10-06T00:00:01Z, and the same within one UTC day.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:TEST-UNIT-05

findings.title: verifyTurnstile's outgoing siteverify request is never asserted: in CI nothing pins the URL, the body fields or the remoteip rule
findings.evidence: reply() stubs fetch with `vi.fn(async () => new Response(...))` and no test reads fetch.mock.calls. The URL, the method and the body `{secret, response, remoteip}` built at turnstile.ts:76-85 are therefore unpinned, as are the omission of remoteip for 'local' (line 82) and the 5 s timeout (line 84). The handler tests inject `verify` and never reach this code. The only other check is the local e2e battery, which posts the dummy token to the real siteverify with the test secret (Cloudflare says test secret keys 'Only accept the dummy token, reject real tokens', developers.cloudflare.com/turnstile/troubleshooting/testing/), and CI does not run it.
findings.impact: A refactor that sends the wrong field as `response`, drops `secret`, or sends remoteip:'local' passes lint, typecheck and the unit suite in CI. It is caught only if someone runs the local e2e battery before deploying. Otherwise every form on the hosted site answers every visitor with 400 or 503: checkout, contact, recovery and sign-ups.
findings.proposed_fix: In the success test, keep the stub and assert one call to 'https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/siteverify' with method POST and the JSON body {secret: REAL_SECRET, response: 'tok', remoteip: '203.0.113.7'}. Add a case with remoteIp 'local' that asserts the body has no remoteip key.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:TEST-UNIT-07

findings.title: The backup reader's own refusals (unsafe path, duplicate, manifest first, size/sha256) are never exercised; only the writer's are
findings.evidence: Every archive the tests read is made by writeBackup, which already refuses an unsafe path (test at line 324). EntryExtractor's own checks in scripts/lib/backup-format.mjs therefore never see bad input: assertSafeEntryPath(meta.path) at line 398, 'Duplicate entry path' at 403-405, 'The first entry must be manifest.json' at 399-401, the impossible header length at 354, and the size/sha256 comparison at 420-422. A grep of tests/ for those messages finds nothing. The tamper tests (lines 195-239) all fail earlier, at gunzip or at the GCM tag, as WRONG_PASSPHRASE_OR_DAMAGED. The header comment says assertSafeEntryPath is 'used by both the writer and the reader'; only its use by the writer is proven.
findings.impact: Deleting line 398, or the duplicate check, in a refactor keeps the suite green, and `pnpm restore-check --extract` would then write an entry named `../x` or `C:/...` outside the chosen directory. Exploiting it needs an archive sealed with the owner's passphrase, because GCM authenticates every byte. The realistic case is a backup file handed to the owner, not a remote attack, and the reader's checks are the last guard against exactly that case.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a test helper that seals a hand-built entry stream with the format's own header, gzip and AES-256-GCM (a few lines with node:crypto and node:zlib, using deriveKey). Assert that readBackup refuses with code CORRUPT and leaves nothing behind for: the entry paths '../escape.txt', 'a\\b' and 'C:/x'; a duplicate path; a first entry that is not manifest.json; a size that does not match; a wrong sha256.

findings.title: cart.test.ts depends on test order through the module's writeFailed and memoryCart state
findings.evidence: src/lib/cart.ts keeps `let memoryCart` (line 233) and `let writeFailed` (line 236) at module level, and readCart returns the memory cart with persistent:false whenever writeFailed is true (line 271). The test 'falls back to memory when setItem throws mid-session' (line 180) leaves writeFailed set to true. The file never resets it (no beforeEach, no vi.resetModules); the later tests pass only because each happens to begin with a successful write. 'persists through a working storage area and discards a malformed value' (line 161) starts with `expect(readCart(area)).toEqual({ cart: EMPTY_CART, persistent: true })`, which fails if it runs after line 180: it would get {cart: [VARIANT_B x1], persistent: false}. store-availability.test.ts:149-152 shows the pattern this file lacks (`vi.resetModules()` and a fresh import).
findings.impact: The suite is green only in declaration order. Running `vitest --sequence.shuffle`, filtering to a single test with .only, or moving a test makes cart tests fail for reasons unrelated to the change, and a real regression in the storage fallback can be masked or blamed on the wrong change. No product impact.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a beforeEach that re-imports the module after vi.resetModules(), as store-availability.test.ts does, or one that performs a successful writeCart(EMPTY_CART, memoryArea()) to clear writeFailed and memoryCart before every test.

findings.title: The test:db guard accepts any loopback Postgres, so three integration files would run against another project's local stack on the same port
findings.evidence: `if (mode === 'db') assertLocalTestDatabase()` checks only that TEST_ENV is 'local' and that the DATABASE_URL host is loopback (src/lib/env.ts:14-29). tests/integration/support.ts:26-34 additionally requires this project's `supabase status`, but buyer-retention.test.ts:13-15, cron-jobs.test.ts:14-16 and static-site.test.ts:12-14 do not import support.ts. They connect to `process.env.DATABASE_URL ?? 'postgresql://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:54322/postgres'`. Port 54322 is the default every local Supabase project uses, and the brief for this audit records that 54321-54324 currently belong to another project's stack.
findings.impact: If `pnpm test:db` is started while another project's stack holds the ports, the files that use support.ts fail at import, but those three connect to the other project's database as `postgres`. Today they only read the catalog or write inside transactions they roll back, so the result is confusing failures, not damage. A future standalone file that commits would write into the other project's local data, which the guard's comment ('a disposable local PostgreSQL instance') says cannot happen.
findings.proposed_fix: In assertLocalTestDatabase, or in a shared helper the three files use, also require a marker that only this project's schema has, e.g. `select to_regprocedure('finance.buyer_retention_purge()') is not null`. Alternatively, derive the URL from `supabase status -o json` (DB_URL), as support.ts does for the API.

findings.title: 'writes only columns the migration grants' compares the table configs with a hand-copied list, not with the migrations
findings.evidence: `const GRANTED: Record<TableKey, readonly string[]> = { products: [...], variants: [...], ... }` is typed into the test (according to its comment, 'read out of' 20260927160000_catalog_and_checkout.sql and 20261002100000_payment_core.sql), and the it.each at line 381 checks each config's toRow keys against that list. Today the copy matches the grants (catalog_and_checkout.sql:264-332 and payment_core.sql:69-71, checked by hand), but a later migration that revokes or adds a column grant leaves the test green. The P07 acceptance record cites the test as proof: artifacts/acceptance/P07/commands.txt:90-91 '... and a unit test proving every config writes only granted columns.'
findings.impact: The test name suggests the forms are proven against the database's grants; they are only proven against the test's own list. A drift would show up only as a 42501 when the owner saves a product, a variant or a coupon (and in the store-admin e2e, if it is run).
findings.proposed_fix: Read the column lists from the migrations, the way scripts/lib/cron-jobs.mjs reads cron.schedule calls (the last grant or revoke per table and column wins). Alternatively, move the assertion to a test:db test that queries information_schema.column_privileges for `authenticated`.

findings.title: 'compares each bucket with the restored database's own rows' only greps the script's source text
findings.evidence: The test reads scripts/restore-check.mjs as text and asserts `toMatch(/group by bucket_id/)` and `toMatch(/object rows in the restored database/)`. The comparison it names is at restore-check.mjs:457-464: the loop `for (const bucket of new Set([...BUCKETS, ...objects.perBucket.keys(), ...bucketRows.keys()]))` and its ok/FAIL decision for each bucket. Any change to that logic that keeps the SQL string and the message (an inverted condition, a bucket dropped from the set) still passes. The test at line 37 does the same for `file_size_limit`.
findings.impact: The test name tells a reader the per-bucket check is proven, but it is not. The real proof is the owner's restore rehearsal (D35), which needs Docker and is run rarely, so a broken check could let a backup without the paid files pass `pnpm restore-check`.
findings.proposed_fix: Move the per-bucket decision into a pure exported function (inputs: BUCKETS, the verified and total counts per bucket, the restored row counts; output: the list of problems). Unit-test it with a missing paid-files bucket, an empty bucket and a count mismatch, and keep the source grep only if it still adds something.

findings.title: The Riyadh-time tests prove nothing on the owner's machine: run in Asia/Riyadh, they pass with the timeZone option deleted; only UTC CI catches it
findings.evidence: The machine's time zone is Asia/Riyadh (node: resolvedOptions().timeZone is 'Asia/Riyadh', offset -180), and vitest.config.ts pins no TZ. format.test.ts:17-20 expects formatDate('2026-09-23T22:30:00Z') to match /24/. A scratch copy of formatDate (src/lib/format.ts:24-32) without `timeZone: 'Asia/Riyadh'` gives «24 سبتمبر 2026» in the machine's zone, so the test passes, and «23 سبتمبر 2026» under TZ=UTC, so it fails (script: SCRATCH/TEST-UNIT/tz-demo.cjs). The same holds for format.test.ts:119-123 (formatRiyadh '2:45 م') and cart.test.ts:452-458 (formatRiyadhTime '14:35'): each is meaningful only when the process zone is not Riyadh.
findings.impact: The acceptance gate the orchestrator runs locally (`pnpm check`) cannot see a dropped or wrong time zone in the three formatters that every date on the site and in the admin goes through; only the Linux CI run after the commit would find it. A buyer or the owner would then see the previous day's date for anything published or paid between 00:00 and 03:00 Riyadh time.
findings.proposed_fix: Pin the unit run to a zone far from Riyadh so these tests mean the same everywhere: e.g. set `process.env.TZ = 'America/Los_Angeles'` at the top of vitest.config.ts (the fork workers inherit it), or use `test.env: { TZ: 'America/Los_Angeles' }`. A western zone also exposes date-only strings that are parsed as local time.

plan_gaps.title: Run the database suite (or its SQL-only files) in CI
plan_gaps.why_needed: CI runs `pnpm test` only (.github/workflows/ci.yml, closing comment). Every unit test of an Edge Function scripts the SQL replies (payments, checkout, download, notify, orders, admin), and their headers point to tests/integration for the real invariants: deny-by-default RLS, finance isolation, the owner and TOTP gates with real JWTs, apply_verified_payment's amount, currency and mode checks, the refund balance, and idempotency. Those run only when someone runs `pnpm test:db` locally, so a regression in a migration or in an authorization line merges green (see TEST-UNIT-03, -05 and -06). The CI job already starts Postgres, PostgREST, Auth and Storage for the build, so the SQL-only files (no edge runtime, no Mailpit) could run there at small cost.

findings.title: No test can see content hidden by opacity or clip-path, so the non-negotiable "no home section hidden behind JS" is unproven
findings.evidence: VERIFICATION.md:23 lists "no home section hidden behind JS" among the non-negotiable invariants. For / with JavaScript off the suite has only public.spec.ts:161-163 (h1 toHaveCount(1) and `expect(await page.locator('main p').count()).toBeGreaterThan(3)`, a DOM count that also counts display:none) and visual.spec.ts:67 (`await expect(page.locator('h1')).toBeVisible()`); no-js.spec.ts never opens /. Playwright counts opacity:0 as visible (playwright.dev/docs/actionability: "Elements with opacity:0 are considered visible"). Measured in Chromium 153 (scratch measure/visible-hidden.cjs): isVisible() is true for opacity:0, for clip-path: inset(100% 0 0 0) and for opacity:0 + translateY(32px), the start states src/components/weave/motion.ts FROM uses.
findings.impact: A change that leaves a home section, or any reveal, at its hidden start state until a script runs (or forever) passes public.spec, visual.spec and no-js.spec; visitors without JavaScript, and everyone when a reveal never plays, would see blank bands while the acceptance battery is green. Today motion.css keeps content visible without JS, so this is a missing proof, not a live defect.
findings.proposed_fix: In the JS-off tests (and one with motion on), wait for document.getAnimations() to finish, then assert for every main section, [data-enter] and [data-reveal] that computed opacity is 1, clip-path is none or inset(0px), visibility is visible and the box is non-empty; run it on / and every room.

findings.title: readCodeFromMailpit returns the newest mail without knowing whether it is the new one, so a second sign-in of the same address can submit the spent code
findings.evidence: helpers.ts:163-172 searches `to:<email>`, takes `messages?.[0]` (Mailpit sorts search results by received date, descending: github.com/axllent/mailpit server/apiv1/messages.go:214) and returns its first `\b\d{6}\b` unless it equals `previousCode`. signInByCode (333-341) forwards previousCode only when a caller passes it. store-admin.spec.ts signs the same `owner.email` in five times without it (lines 89, 214, 236, 275, 370), cms.spec.ts twice (666, 677). SignIn.tsx:41-52 shows the same SENT sentence for every answer except a lost connection and a 429, so a masked failure (an SMTP or server error) also reads as sent.
findings.impact: When the new mail is not yet the newest message for the address (late hand-off to Mailpit) or was never sent (a masked non-429 failure), the helper returns the previous, already used code: the test fails at `toHaveURL(/\/admin$/)` with no hint that the code was stale, a flake that reads like a sign-in regression.
findings.proposed_fix: Before clicking «أرسل الرمز», record the ID of the newest message for the address and wait for a newer one; make signInByCode always do it instead of relying on callers to pass previousCode.
findings.prior_overlap: none

The refresh (864-872) and download (442-450) checks of the same file do re-count after the answer; this one does not.

coverage:
Read in full: playwright.config.ts; .github/workflows/ci.yml; package.json; tsconfig.json; vitest.config.ts; all 19 files of tests/e2e (auth, cart-checkout, checkout-api, cms, helpers, media, motion, no-js, order-page, orders-admin, orders-money, orders, owner-operations, product-availability, public, reader, shots, store-admin, visual); docs/development.md; PLANS/VERIFICATION.md; PLANS/ISSUES.md open items; HANDOFF.md:32; tests/integration/support.ts (harness setup and stop); tests/support/moyasar-emulator.ts (config, reset, redirects); the migrations behind the screens the specs assert on (staff_directory, order_access, order_summary, payment_view, outbox_claim, contact_submit, orders_alerts, refund_result); scripts/check-export.mjs, check-budgets.mjs, local-env.mjs; P08 round-12a record; AUDIT-1 TESTS.json; AUDIT-2 findings for e2e/CI; DESIGN-B commands.txt.

What each spec drives: auth (code sign-in, TOTP enrolment, invite through step-up; no denial cases, refuted in AUDIT-2 GAP-G1-12); public (one h1 and no console errors on 10 routes, menu, skip link, films, scenes filter and lightbox, contact validation, JS-off as DOM counts); no-js (header inline at 375, scenes links, journal, contact noscript, P08 pages offer no dead control; all under reduced motion); motion (counts Element.animate calls per element; proves reveals are scheduled and played, not that content ends visible); visual (13 routes x 4 widths, overflow <= 1px end side only, captures never compared; JS-off h1 only); cart-checkout/checkout-api (real quote/create/pay/cancel against the emulator; refusal and verify states partly mocked); orders (10 journeys x 2 widths on the real stack and emulator, no page.route: verified); order-page (order and notify pages, functions fully mocked; mock shapes match order_access/order_summary/payment_view and download refusals); product-availability (catalog_availability and notify mocked, quote patched, one real read); orders-admin/orders-money (real sign-in and harness-made orders; orders-money mocks every admin function reply, reconciliation lists mocked); store-admin (P07 admin CRUD, the switch with step-up, 11c preorder/paid file/sign-ups/stats against real functions with targeted mocks); owner-operations (contact/outbox/webhook/sweep at HTTP level, home, email problems, settings); cms, media, reader (real stack; reader PDF fixtures routed).

Mock policy: page.route fakes function or Data API answers in order-page, product-availability, orders-money, orders-admin, store-admin, cart-checkout and reader (inventory in my grep); orders.spec, checkout-api, cms, media, owner-operations, auth, public, no-js, motion and visual use none. Spot-checked mock fidelity (orders get, download, payments verify, admin STEP_UP_REQUIRED): faithful.

Widths: visual 360/768/1024/1440 (heights 1000, not the plan's 800/1024/768/900); P08 specs 360 and 1440; no-js 375; public menu 375/1280; reader 1440/390/360/900; media and admin screenshots 360/1440; none at 320, no zoom. Overflow of story pages is measured only under reduced motion.

CI: a green run proves lint errors (a11y rules are warnings), types (including the specs), unit tests, frozen sources, copy rules, Deno types, that every migration applies to a fresh Postgres, the content import, a static export with the 59 required files and no secret shape, RTL attributes and the JS budget of the pages that exist without products or posts. It proves nothing about RLS, grants, money SQL, functions at runtime, mail, payments or any browser journey; test:db and e2e never run there (confirmed) and cannot run against a hosted deployment. No automated link between a tested commit and the hosted site exists (plan gap).

Emulator's part: the journeys prove the code against the emulator's reading of Moyasar's docs, including faults; its stand-in page redirects to success_url verbatim, so orders.spec.ts:294's `\?order=N$` bakes in a choice Moyasar's docs leave open (P08 docs record), while the return page's tolerance of appended params is proven separately (cart-checkout.spec.ts:892-917, 1057-1065). Real invoice pages, webhook headers/retries and live behaviour stay under E02.

Mailpit retrieval: newest-first is correct; the stale-code race is TEST-E2E-05. 1,000 staff rows: a product truncation in staff_directory (TEST-E2E-03), plus pile-up from helpers that never retire users.

Measurements (scratch audit/TEST-E2E/measure): overflow-clip.cjs, visible-hidden.cjs, pdf-text.mjs. Nothing in the repo was run or changed; no request went to ports 54320-54329.

Lead disposition: lead TEST-E2E-01 (team screen truncation) confirmed as TEST-E2E-03 (its line 76 is 71). The previous attempt had no other leads.

Not reached or left for more time: host.docker.internal mapping by Supabase CLI 2.106.0 on Linux runners (needed for the full CI step); per-mock shape fidelity for the reconciliation_list, disputes_list and admin stats mocks; whether GoTrue rejects a reused TOTP code within its step (orders.spec answers several step-ups quickly); a timing run of test:db for the CI estimate.

findings.title: AUDIT-1 S22.1 regressed: EXECUTION-STATUS's Current state table says P08 waits for round 12a and its lock, two rounds after both were committed
findings.evidence: Line 11: "P08 in progress (rounds 0 to 11c accepted and pushed; paused after 11c ...; 12a, 12b, checkpoint (c), the battery and the plan documents left"; line 10 "Last commit | P08 round 11c d27d05b"; line 12 "It is taken again for round 12a". git log shows 75a845f (round 12a) and 3a30a91 (round 12b) committed; the same file's P08 row (361) and Next work (369) say every round through 12b is built. `git show 3a30a91 -- PLANS/EXECUTION-STATUS.md` changed only the hunks at 358 and 366

findings.title: The AUDIT-1 X1.1 policy reset closes a live store silently: nothing alerts the owner and his settings screen still says «الشراء مفتوح»
findings.evidence: policies_reset_approval sets `policy_revisions = '{}'` and only `insert into public.audit_events (... 'commerce.policies_reset' ...)` (lines 141-149); it neither turns checkout_enabled off nor calls finance.owner_alert (P08's alert mail, 20261002100000_payment_core.sql:420). From then on checkout_quote reports `'checkoutEnabled', v_settings.checkout_enabled and ... and v_settings.policy_revisions <> '{}'` = false (20261002110000_checkout_payment.sql:351-357), so the cart and checkout say «الشراء غير متاح حاليًا، ويفتح قريبًا.», and checkout_create answers POLICIES_NOT_CONFIGURED (459-460). The owner's screen reads the raw flag: CommerceSettingsForm.tsx:251 `{row.checkoutEnabled ? 'الشراء مفتوح' : 'الشراء مغلق'}`; AdminHome.tsx has no store-state line at all; the publish bar (src/components/admin/PublishBar.tsx) says nothing about it when the document is a policy, and src/admin/collections/policies.ts:5-6 confirms editors draft and publish policy text
findings.impact: Once the store is open (after E02), any publish of a new seq of an approved policy, by an editor (content_assert_publisher allows owner and editor) or by a scheduled publish at night (publish_due), stops every sale until the owner happens to re-approve with a fresh TOTP. He is never told, and the one screen that shows the switch tells him the store is open; Anas loses sales for as long as nobody notices. The rule itself is intended (docs/operations.md:723-731); the missing signal is the defect, and it only matters now that checkout and payments exist
findings.proposed_fix: In policies_reset_approval, after the audit insert, add `perform finance.owner_alert('policies_reset', v_doc || ':' || coalesce(v_seq::text, 'removed'), jsonb_build_object('policy', v_doc))` with a one-line Arabic template in the order-mail renderer; and in CommerceSettingsForm show «الشراء مغلق حتى تُعتمد السياسات» when checkoutEnabled is true and no revision is approved
findings.proof_recipe: On the local stack with checkout on and policies approved: `select policy_revisions, checkout_enabled from finance.commerce_settings` (non-empty, true); as an editor JWT insert a new content_versions row for ('policies','refund') and `select public.publish_version('policies','refund',<new seq>)`; then `select policy_revisions, checkout_enabled from finance.commerce_settings` -> '{}' and still true; `select count(*) from finance.email_outbox where kind = 'owner_alert' and created_at > now() - interval '1 minute'` -> 0 (wrong: the owner should be told); POST checkout quote -> checkoutEnabled false while /admin/settings shows «الشراء مفتوح»

findings.title: AUDIT-1 G4.6 half fixed: the graft hook helper still falls back to importing <project>/dist/claude/hooks.js
findings.evidence: entry(): `return path.join(dir, 'dist', 'claude', name); // last-ditch` with `const dir = process.env.CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR || process.cwd()` (line 6), then line 67 `import(pathToFileURL(entry("hooks.js")).href)`. The settings half of G4.6 holds (no `node dist/cli.js` or `graft-dev` allow entries), but git log --all -- .claude/helpers/graft-hooks.cjs shows only the 8ffdb9c baseline: the hook change the fix prescribed was never committed
findings.impact: On a machine where graft is not found through the baked path, the project's node_modules, node's lib or the npm global root, every Claude Code hook in this repository imports and runs <repo>/dist/claude/hooks.js without a prompt; dist/ is not git-ignored, so a file committed there by a branch or a tool would run in the owner's sessions. Exploitability is low while the global graft install exists

findings.title: AUDIT-1 S04.1's costs note went stale with P08's three tiers: availability notices now stop at 50, not 80

Since 20261002120000_order_emails.sql:323 the claim is `v_sent_today < p_daily_quota - case o.priority when 0 then 0 when 1 then p_reserve else p_reserve + p_low_reserve end`; availability and notify_confirm are priority 2 (20261002150000_notifications.sql:117,380) and outbox.ts sets LOW_RESERVE = 30, so they stop at 100 - 20 - 30 = 50; order_link (priority 1) is new and absent from the note

findings.title: Physical orders take a free-text address with no National Address, which Saudi parcel carriers must refuse since 2026-01-01
findings.evidence: The only address input is `<label htmlFor="checkout-address">عنوان التوصيل</label>` with a 500-character textarea (CheckoutForm.tsx:713-727); `checkout_create` accepts any 5 to 500 characters without control characters (supabase/migrations/20261002110000_checkout_payment.sql:519-521) and snapshots it as `orders.address`. The Transport General Authority's decision, effective Thursday 2026-01-01: «إلزام كافة شركات نقل الطرود بعدم استلام أو نقل أي شحنة بريدية لا تتضمن العنوان الوطني» (Okaz, 2025-12-28, https://www.okaz.com.sa/local/na/2228688). D09, DATA-AND-SECURITY and E03 mention city rates and manual carriers only; no plan document mentions the National Address.
findings.impact: Every paid physical or signed order whose buyer typed a street description instead of his National Address cannot be handed to a carrier until Anas reaches the buyer; a parcel stuck past 15 days lets the buyer cancel under the E-Commerce Law's article 14 (owner must confirm), and a refund follows.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a required «العنوان الوطني المختصر» field (or the National Address parts the chosen carrier asks for) to the physical part of the checkout, validated in the quote, `checkout_create` and the order snapshot and shown on the order view; fix the exact fields with Anas's carrier (E03, Q38).

findings.title: No public page names the seller: the store shows no seller name, registration, address or contact means, which the E-Commerce Law asks an e-store to disclose
findings.evidence: The seller's legal name, address and registration exist only in `finance.commerce_settings` (owner-only; src/components/admin/CommerceSettingsForm.tsx:183-215) and in order snapshots; a grep for seller fields in src/components/store, src/components/site and src/app/(public) finds none, and the store page renders only the title band and product cards (store/page.tsx:25-71). The receipt adds only «البائع» and «رقم التسجيل» (supabase/functions/_shared/email.ts:377-383), not the address or a delivery date. E-Commerce Law (https://laws.boe.gov.sa/BoeLaws/Laws/LawDetails/360de590-0286-4fa5-a243-aa9100c31979/1, read 2026-10-07): article 6, the provider discloses in its e-store its name or distinguishing mark, its address (unless registered with an authentication body), its means of contact and its register details; article 8, an invoice after the contract with each item's cost, the total with fees and delivery, and the delivery date and place. No plan document mentions either article.
findings.impact: When checkout opens, the store sells under a name and address no buyer can see before paying, and Moyasar's pre-live review looks at 'communication channels' (FAQ). Whether a published seller block or the Saudi Business Center's free e-commerce authentication certificate (which would spare publishing a home address) is required for a freelance-document seller is for the owner to confirm; this is not legal advice.
findings.proposed_fix: Before checkout opens, decide with Anas (and an adviser if needed) what the store discloses; add a seller block (name, registration, address or authentication number, contact means, complaints channel) to the store and policy pages, fed by a public CMS field or a published copy of the seller settings; add the delivery address and expected date to the receipt of physical orders.
findings.prior_overlap: none

findings.title: The non-negotiable 'no runtime DDL' invariant has no test, and table deny-by-default has no catalog-wide test (only functions do)
findings.evidence: PLANS/VERIFICATION.md:22 requires 'Direct SQL tests separately prove deny-by-default public access, `finance` isolation, server-only functions executable by `service_role` alone, and no runtime DDL.' A grep of tests/integration, tests/unit and tests/e2e for has_schema_privilege, pg_class, relrowsecurity, pg_default_acl, 'ddl' or any CREATE check finds nothing. The only catalog-wide check is S01.5 (audit-fixes.test.ts:107-142), which enumerates pg_proc for PUBLIC and anon EXECUTE only; tables are checked one by one per file (checkout.test.ts:810-833, payment.test.ts:484, forms.test.ts:197).
findings.impact: A future migration that grants a table to anon/authenticated without RLS, grants CREATE on public or finance to an API role, or adds dynamic DDL in a security-definer function passes the whole suite; the acceptance gate claims a proof that does not exist. No current breach was found (no `execute format` in the migrations; 20260924130000:7-12 revokes table defaults for anon/authenticated).
findings.proposed_fix: Add one catalog test beside S01.5: (a) has_schema_privilege(r, s, 'CREATE') is false for r in anon, authenticated, service_role and s in public, finance; (b) every public/finance table on which anon or authenticated holds a privilege has relrowsecurity = true, and the set of (role, table, privilege) equals a committed allow-list; (c) has_schema_privilege(anon|authenticated, 'finance', 'USAGE') is false.
findings.proof_recipe: To see whether the property itself holds today: select r, has_schema_privilege(r,'public','CREATE') pub, has_schema_privilege(r,'finance','CREATE') fin, has_schema_privilege(r,'finance','USAGE') fin_usage from unnest(array['anon','authenticated','service_role']) r; any true in pub/fin breaks 'no runtime DDL', a true fin_usage for anon/authenticated breaks finance isolation.

findings.title: The coupon-limit race test cannot fail without the coupon lock: both carts hold the same variant, whose row lock already serializes the two creates
findings.evidence: checkout.test.ts:1123-1137 races two creates whose carts are both `[{ variantId: variant, quantity: 1 }]` with one coupon of usage_limit 1. checkout_create locks the cart's variants first and the coupon second (20261002110000_checkout_payment.sql:507 `perform 1 from public.product_variants v where v.id = any(v_ids) order by v.id for update;`, :509 `perform 1 from public.coupons c where c.code = v_code for update;`) and only then counts uses (:512 checkout_price -> finance.coupon_uses). The second create waits on the shared variant row until the first commits and sees its held redemption whether or not line 509 exists. The loser may also answer QUOTE_CHANGED, which a purely sequential run produces.
findings.impact: VERIFICATION.md:25 lists 'true simultaneous last-stock/coupon requests' as non-negotiable, and the coupon row lock is the only guard of a usage limit (coupon_redemptions has no count constraint, unlike refunds' refunds_in_flight_* indexes). Dropping or reordering that lock lets two buyers of different products redeem a limited coupon past its limit with the suite green; payment then commits both by design (payment.test.ts:1612).
findings.proposed_fix: Race two carts with different variants and the same limited coupon, forced: h.holdLock('select 1 from public.coupons where id = $1 for update'), start both creates, assert both 'blocked' via settledWithin, release, expect exactly one ok and the other COUPON_EXHAUSTED.
findings.proof_recipe: On a scratch local database re-create public.checkout_create without line 509; run `vitest run --mode db tests/integration/checkout.test.ts -t 'coupon limited to one use'`: it still passes (expected wrong result). The two-variant forced version fails without line 509 and passes with it.

findings.title: HTTP integration tests run against whatever code the edge runtime last loaded; nothing detects a stale runtime

findings.impact: A change under supabase/functions/_shared that breaks the webhook, checkout, refund or download path passes `pnpm test:db` when the restart is forgotten: unit tests import the new code, the HTTP tests prove the old, and the P08 money invariants get false acceptance evidence. A writer is editing _shared/payments.ts in the working tree during this audit, which is exactly that situation.
findings.proposed_fix: In support.ts, the first time FUNCTIONS_URL is used, compare `docker inspect -f '{{.State.StartedAt}}' supabase_edge_runtime_<project_id>` with the newest mtime under supabase/functions and throw 'restart the edge runtime' when a file is newer; or make the test:db script restart the container first.

findings.title: The local-only guard checks only that DATABASE_URL is loopback; nothing ties it to the stack `supabase status` reports, and three spec files never consult that stack
findings.evidence: assertLocalTestDatabase() requires TEST_ENV === 'local' and a host in LOCAL_HOSTS ('localhost', '127.0.0.1', '::1', '[::1]', 'host.docker.internal') (env.ts:38-51, _shared/env.ts:57). support.ts applies the loopback rule to the API host only (support.ts:1-4, 26-34); its pg helpers use `process.env.DATABASE_URL ?? 'postgresql://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:54322/postgres'` (support.ts:173, 188, 243, 406) without comparing it to status.DB_URL. buyer-retention.test.ts, cron-jobs.test.ts and static-site.test.ts do not import support.ts (grep -L "from './support'").
findings.impact: Any loopback Postgres passes: another project's local stack on 54322 (the case on this machine today) or a port-forward to a hosted database. Those three files write only inside rolled-back transactions, so no data loss was found; but a mixed run (API from this stack, SQL to another database) reports on the wrong database, and the helpers never refuse on their own.
findings.proposed_fix: In support.ts read status.DB_URL and throw unless DATABASE_URL has the same host and port; replace the hard-coded fallbacks with the checked URL; import the same check in the three files that skip support.ts.

findings.title: outbox.test.ts re-dates every other pending, uncertain or sending mail in the shared database and never restores it
findings.evidence: parkOthers(): `update finance.email_outbox set next_at = now() + interval '1 day', first_attempt_at = now() - interval '2 days' where dedupe_key not like $1 and status in ('pending', 'uncertain', 'sending')`, committed and called by 17 tests; afterAll (29-32) restores nothing. email-delivery.test.ts:239-245 does the same to every foreign due row; order-emails.test.ts:1129 pushes every other pending/uncertain row a day out (next_at only).
findings.impact: Foreign uncertain/sending rows are pushed past the 23-hour idempotency window (first_attempt_at two days ago), so the claim never retries them and they need a person's duplicate-risk replay; pending mail of a dev session or e2e run is delayed a day; which rows are hit depends on file order.
findings.proposed_fix: Record the ids and old (next_at, first_attempt_at) of parked rows and restore them in afterAll, or park only rows created before the file started and only next_at.
findings.prior_overlap: R2-08 (artifacts/acceptance/P08/rounds/round-02.md:84, payment.test.ts parkAll; recorded, not changed). This copy also rewrites first_attempt_at.

findings.title: The append-only rule for audit_events has no test: no spec ever updates or deletes an audit row

No test in tests/integration, tests/unit or tests/e2e updates or deletes an audit row, so the trigger never fires in the suite; disputes have the equivalent test (stats.test.ts:1103).
findings.impact: A migration that drops or replaces the trigger (for example to let an erase redact actors) leaves every test green; the C23 'append-only audit' claim rests on reading the migration.
findings.proposed_fix: Copy stats.test.ts:1103: as the migration role, update and delete of an audit fixture row both raise 42501 in a rolled-back transaction; the owner's Data API update/delete is refused.

findings.title: No test presents a tampered JWT: the owner step-up (aal2, fresh TOTP) that guards refunds, disputes and the commerce settings is proven only with genuine tokens
findings.evidence: The step-up lives only in the Edge Functions (admin.ts:225-248 `if (!staff.recentTotp) ...`; SQL cannot see aal/amr), and staffFromRequest (supabase/functions/_shared/staff.ts:36) trusts `client.auth.getClaims(token)`. Every refusal test uses a real session: a stale owner (disputes-http.test.ts:186, refunds-http.test.ts:758), editor/operations, no bearer, or the literal 'not-a-jwt' (stats.test.ts:116, in-process). No test anywhere re-signs or edits a JWT.
findings.impact: If verify_jwt were turned off for admin or staffFromRequest changed to decode without verifying, a token whose payload was edited to aal 'aal2' with a fresh 'totp' amr would move money and nothing in test:db or e2e would notice. Today both layers verify (config.toml:449-453; getClaims per the vendor docs), so no exploit exists.
findings.proposed_fix: Take a real aal1 owner token, rewrite its payload (aal 'aal2', amr [{method:'totp', timestamp: now}]) keeping the old signature, and also sign one with a random HS256 key; send both to admin dispute-record over HTTP and to handleAdmin in-process; expect 401 and nothing written.
findings.proof_recipe: POST /functions/v1/admin {action:'dispute-record', ...} with the edited token: expected 401 (201/200 means the step-up is bypassable).

findings.title: Four functions any signed-in session can execute have no refusal test: schedule_version, archive_document, cancel_schedule (never called at all) and media_product_usage
findings.evidence: All four are security definer and granted to authenticated (static-site.test.ts:47-52 checks grants only; 20260927180000_store_media.sql:46-47). Their role checks (content_assert_publisher in 20260930120000_audit_fixes.sql:222-231 and 20260930140000_audit2_fixes.sql:204-213, 242-252; current_staff_role() in store_media.sql:36-38) are exercised for refusal only through publish_version (publish.test.ts:99-115, operations -> 42501). A reachability pass over the 159 final functions finds cancel_schedule and media_product_usage called by no integration test; e2e reaches them only on the owner/editor happy path (cms.spec.ts:178, the MediaLibrary selection).
findings.impact: If one body lost its publisher check, an operations member or a revoked member with a live session could unschedule, schedule or archive public content (archiving an approved policy also closes checkout, X1.1) or read draft product titles, with the suite green.
findings.proposed_fix: Extend publish.test.ts:99 to call schedule_version, archive_document and cancel_schedule as operations and as an inactive editor through the Data API, expecting 42501 and nothing changed; add media_product_usage beside media_where_used in media-security.test.ts:457.

findings.title: The privacy of the paid files (and the private originals) is proven only from catalog text: a broad storage policy that never names the bucket passes, and nothing tries to read a private object without a signed URL
findings.evidence: The check is `select count(*) from pg_policies where schemaname = 'storage' and tablename = 'objects' and (coalesce(qual,'') || ' ' || coalesce(with_check,'')) like '%paid-files%'` = 0 plus `public: false` (payment.test.ts:625-641); media-private gets only the bucket row (static-site.test.ts:92-112). Every Storage read of a paid object in tests uses serviceClient (orders-http.test.ts:254, 511, 536; download.test.ts:542) or a signed URL; no test lists or downloads paid-files or media-private as anon or a signed-in session.
findings.impact: A later policy such as `for select to authenticated using (true)` or `using (bucket_id <> 'media-public')` would let a signed-in session list `assets/<variant>/` and download Anas's paid PDFs and EPUBs without buying them, and the test would still pass. The migrations create no storage.objects policy today, so nothing is exposed now.
findings.proposed_fix: Assert the stronger invariant that holds today (no policy on storage.objects, or an explicit allow-list) and add a runtime probe: anonClient() and a signed-in editor call storage.from('paid-files').list('assets') and .download(<fixture key>) and get nothing; GET /storage/v1/object/public/paid-files/<key> is not 200; the same for media-private originals.

findings.title: A contact-form flood fills the whole priority-1 mail band P08 now shares with order_link, holding every order-recovery link to the next UTC day
findings.evidence: AUDIT-2's DB-contacts-2 fix sized contact_submit's daily cap to the band: «40 a day is at most 80 notices with two recipients» (20260930140000_audit2_fixes.sql:414-422, `rate_limit_take('contact:all', …, 40, interval '1 day')`). P08 then put `order_link` into the same tier (P08-CONTRACT.md section 8: priority 1 = contact_notice and order_link, sent while the day's sends are under 80), and round 5's R5-01 ruling removed any claim-level contact cap. The claim gates by the day's total and orders FIFO: `and v_sent_today < p_daily_quota - case o.priority when 0 then 0 when 1 then p_reserve else …` (:323) / `order by o.priority, o.next_at, o.id` (:327); contact notices are queued one per active owner or operations member (audit2_fixes.sql:457-462) and order links at priority 1 (20261002140000_delivery.sql:253). With two recipients, 40 Turnstile-passing messages queue 80 notices; the dispatcher claims up to CLAIM_LIMIT 10 a minute (supabase/functions/_shared/outbox.ts:65), so the 80-send band is spent within minutes and no priority-1 row is claimed again until 00:00 UTC.
findings.impact: Precondition: two or more active owner/operations recipients and someone willing to pass Turnstile 40 times a day (5 an hour per IP, 3 an hour per address, 40 a day in total). Then every buyer who asks «استعادة رابط الطلب» that day (the only way back to a paid order and its download once the mailed 7-day link has expired) gets the link only after midnight UTC, and the same happens each day the flood repeats; real visitors' contact notices wait too. Bounded to about a day per message; no money or data is lost.
findings.proposed_fix: Keep part of the band for the recovery links: let contact notices claim only while the day's sends are under p_daily_quota - p_reserve - 20 (or under the band minus the links still allowed today, 20 - v_link_today), so order_link's own 20-a-day cap always has room; add a two-recipient case to tests/integration/order-emails.test.ts (80 notices sent today, an order link is still claimed). Alternatively move order_link to priority 0, since it is capped at 20 a day.
findings.prior_overlap: AUDIT-2 DB-contacts-2 (the 40-a-day cap sized to the band); P08 R5-01 (claim-level contact cap removed); not raised in round 5's audit or rulings, nor in wave A
findings.proof_recipe: On a fresh local stack, in one transaction rolled back at the end: move today's sent rows out of the day (update finance.email_outbox set sent_at = now() - interval '2 days' where sent_at >= date_trunc('day', now(), 'UTC')); insert 80 rows kind 'contact_notice', priority 1, status 'pending', next_at now() - interval '1 hour' (recipients = active owners' addresses), and 1 row kind 'order_link', priority 1, status 'pending', next_at now(); loop: select * from public.outbox_claim(1, 120, 100, 20, 3000, 30); for each returned id update finance.email_outbox set status = 'sent', sent_at = now() where id = <id>; stop when nothing is returned. Wrong result: the loop stops after 80 contact notices and the order_link row is still 'pending' (it would be claimed only after 00:00 UTC).

findings.title: The availability sweep's switch-off guard ignores the other closures: a restock during a policy-approval reset mails subscribers who cannot buy, and spends their one notice
findings.evidence: Round 8's orchestrator fix («the sweep told subscribers an item was back while checkout was switched off … It now does nothing at all while the switch is off») checks the stored flag only: `if not coalesce((select s.checkout_enabled from finance.commerce_settings s where s.id = 1), false) then return 0;`. The buyers' gate is wider: checkout_quote and checkout_create also close for an unset seller or an empty policy_revisions (20261002110000_checkout_payment.sql:352-356, :453-461). A subscriber is told once per revision: the sweep sets notified_revision = revision when it queues the mail (:369-374), and the revision moves only on a false→true flip. PLANS/SITE-STATE-CONTRACT.md plans one more condition (site_state = 'open') but not the readiness ones.
findings.impact: While the approval is reset (any republish of an approved policy, FIX-A2-03) a restocked variant still sends «توفّر» mails; the subscriber finds «الشراء غير متاح حاليًا»; when the owner re-approves, the variant is still sellable, the revision does not move and nobody is told again, so the sign-up's promise is spent on a moment nothing could be bought: the case round 8 fixed for the switch.
findings.proposed_fix: Gate the sweep on the same readiness the quote uses: `checkout_enabled and seller_legal_name is not null and seller_registration is not null and policy_revisions <> '{}'::jsonb` (one select of the settings row); add a case to tests/integration/notify.test.ts with the approval emptied.
findings.prior_overlap: P08 round 8, the orchestrator's own finding (sweep while the switch is off); AUDIT-2 I48 (2)

findings.title: Soon/maintenance design B still scrolls 4-17 px at 520-700 px widths: the word's height budget assumes the smallest clamps
findings.evidence: `--F: max(96px, min((100vw - 32px) / 1.676, (var(--h) - 405px) / 1.3));` reserves a fixed 405px for everything but the word, while five vertical clamps grow with the viewport height (.sky padding clamp(20px, h*0.036, 32px), .ground --ft clamp(20px, h*0.038, 30px) and --fb clamp(18px, h*0.044, 34px), .signature margin clamp(10px, h*0.028, 22px), .domain margin clamp(8px, h*0.02, 16px): about 94px at 568 high, about 131px at 800 high). Rendered from disk with reduced motion: /v/b/ and its twin /m/b/ (same stylesheet) give pageH 770 at 520x760, 724 at 540x720, 815 at 600x800, 917 at 700x900; they fit at 320x568, 360x640, 480x800, 600x960 and 760x1000. The MAINT-1 fix «design B fits short screens» and EXECUTION-STATUS's «one screen from 360 wide» therefore do not hold where the word is height-limited (portrait windows between about 500 and 780 px wide). The site files are unchanged since 0b915c5, so the live domain shows the same.
findings.impact: A visitor on a small tablet, a foldable's inner screen or a narrow desktop window sees a page that scrolls by up to 17 px, with the domain line under the fold, on a page designed as one still screen; cosmetic, no content lost.
findings.proposed_fix: Reserve the clamps' upper bound in the height term, for example `(var(--h) - 441px) / 1.3`, or subtract the same clamp() expressions instead of the 405px constant; re-run shots.cjs at 540x720, 600x800 and 700x900.
findings.prior_overlap: MAINT-1 (design B fits short screens); EXECUTION-STATUS SOON-1 row records only design C's 52 px at 320x568

plan_gaps.title: I48 (1)'s approval race (GAP-G5-3) is not closed by P08's built-revision design
plan_gaps.why_needed: P08 closed the static-build half of I48 (1): the checkout sends the revisions the build rendered and waits while they differ from the approved ones (CheckoutForm.tsx:205,313-317; cart.ts builtPolicyRevisions). The race AUDIT-2 GAP-G5-3 named is still in the SQL: commerce_policies_approve (last defined 20260930140000_audit2_fixes.sql:83-141) locks only the settings row and reads published_documents.seq with no lock, and policies_reset_approval (20260930120000_audit_fixes.sql:141-145) resets only when the key is already in policy_revisions, so its UPDATE matches no row and takes no lock when the approval was empty. A policy publish whose transaction overlaps a first approval can leave the approval on the older seq; today that fails closed (every checkout waits with «نحدّث السياسات الآن؛ حاول بعد قليل.» until the owner approves again) and the settings screen lists only approved revisions (CommerceSettingsForm.tsx:170-176), not the live ones. When the plan documents close I48 at P08's end, (1) must not be closed on the built-revision change alone. (The race itself is also reported as findings by wave A DB-CORE-03 and DB-COMMERCE-05; this entry is about the I48 record.)
plan_gaps.touches: a new forward migration (lock the settings row unconditionally in policies_reset_approval, or read the policies' published rows FOR SHARE in commerce_policies_approve); src/components/admin/CommerceSettingsForm.tsx (approved vs live seq); PLANS/ISSUES.md I48

doc_claims_checked.claim: PostgREST retries a function that raises SQLSTATE 40001 instead of answering, so stale-version conflicts must not use 40001 (the premise of AUDIT-1 X2.3 and AUDIT-2 4.1)
doc_claims_checked.evidence: Supabase troubleshooting page «SQLSTATE 40001 (serialization_failure) in an RPC function causes infinite retries» (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/troubleshooting/high-cpu-and-infinite-transaction-retries-when-using-custom-error-codes-in-rpc-functions-77326b): the raise tells PostgREST the failure is transient so it retries the transaction; present in PostgREST 14, fixed in PostgREST 16. The code's 23505 is safe on either version.

doc_claims_checked.claim: The Data API answers unique_violation (23505) with HTTP 409, which the functions map to CONFLICT
doc_claims_checked.evidence: PostgREST error table (https://docs.postgrest.org/en/stable/references/errors.html): 23505 → 409 uniqueness violation; 40* → 500. Same table: 54* (program_limit_exceeded, every throttle here) → 500, not 429; the Edge Functions map the body's code 54000 to 429 themselves, so only a direct Data API caller sees 500.

doc_claims_checked.claim: A Resend send refused with a daily-quota 429 started no idempotency window for its key, so the retry may reuse the key with a re-rendered body (the premise of AUDIT-2 DB-auditfix-3's QUOTA give-back, which clears first_attempt_at and keeps the key)
doc_claims_checked.evidence: Resend's idempotency page (https://resend.com/docs/dashboard/emails/idempotency-keys) says only that keys are kept 24 hours and that a key reused with a different payload answers 409 invalid_idempotent_request; it does not say whether a 429-refused request stores the key. P08 R5-05 records that live-rendered kinds can differ between attempts; if Resend stores the key on a 429, a receipt re-rendered after a quota day would end IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. Worth one sandbox question with the real key.

findings.title: The restore rehearsal loads the whole production database into a stack whose ports Docker publishes on every interface, behind the CLI's public default credentials
findings.evidence: restore-check.mjs:423 runs `supabase start --workdir <scratch>` on the `supabase init` defaults (patchConfig only moves ports +1000 and turns services off), then loads data.sql (auth.users, auth.mfa_factors, every finance and customer row) and uploads every paid file. Supabase CLI v2.106.0 publishes ports with no host IP (apps/cli-go/internal/db/start/start.go:121 `nat.PortBinding{{HostPort: hostPort}}`; internal/start/start.go:556-557 for Kong) and defaults to `Password: "postgres"` (pkg/config/config.go:366) and public API secrets (pkg/config/apikeys.go:17-20, defaultJwtSecret and sb_secret_N7UND…). `docker ps` on this machine shows the running CLI stack as `0.0.0.0:54322->5432/tcp, [::]:54322->5432/tcp`. Docker: ports mapped without a host address are published `to all host addresses (0.0.0.0 and [::])` (https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/port-publishing/); the daemon `ip` default does not apply to user-defined networks such as the CLI's (https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/drivers/bridge/).
findings.impact: For the minutes a rehearsal runs, any device that can reach the owner's machine (home or office Wi-Fi, a café; on Windows when Docker Desktop's firewall prompt was allowed, on macOS by default) can run `psql postgresql://postgres:postgres@<owner-ip>:55322/postgres` and copy every customer, order and address and the owner's TOTP secret, or pull the paid files through the API on 55321 with the stack's default service key. D35 encrypts backups so that this plaintext never leaves the owner's control.
findings.proposed_fix: Before `supabase start`, create the scratch network bound to loopback: `docker network create -o com.docker.network.bridge.host_binding_ipv4=127.0.0.1 supabase_network_anasaq-restore-check` (the CLI reuses an existing network: internal/utils/docker.go:68-71); after start, read `docker port supabase_db_anasaq-restore-check` and refuse to restore unless every binding is 127.0.0.1.
findings.proof_recipe: Run `pnpm restore-check <file>` on a disposable backup; while it prints `Uploading storage objects...`, run `docker port supabase_db_anasaq-restore-check` (wrong result: `5432/tcp -> 0.0.0.0:55322` and `[::]:55322`), then from a second device on the same network `psql postgresql://postgres:postgres@<machine LAN IP>:55322/postgres -c "select count(*) from auth.users"` (wrong result: the restored row count instead of a refused connection).

findings.title: restore-check rehearses a hosted backup on the CLI's default Auth, Storage and Postgres images, not the linked project's versions, so version skew fails a good backup
findings.evidence: Line 419 `supabase init --workdir <tmp>`, line 423 `supabase start --workdir <tmp>`: the scratch project has no supabase/.temp. CLI v2.106.0 pkg/config/config.go:658-675 swaps the Postgres, PostgREST, GoTrue and Storage images (and Storage's target migration) for the linked project's versions only when supabase/.temp/{postgres,rest,gotrue,storage}-version exist; internal/link/link.go:119-167,285 writes them on `supabase link`. The schema dump excludes auth and storage (pkg/migration/dump.go:169 uses InternalSchemas), so those tables come from the scratch images while data.sql's `COPY "auth"."..." (columns)` lists come from the hosted project, and psql runs with ON_ERROR_STOP=1 in one transaction (restore-check.mjs:147-149).
findings.impact: Once the hosted project runs a newer GoTrue or Storage than the images bundled with the owner's CLI (hosted services upgrade continuously; the docs pin the CLI at 2.106.0), a COPY names a column or table the scratch schema lacks, psql stops, and `pnpm restore-check` reports `The psql restore failed` for a backup that would restore into a new hosted project. The owner cannot prove any backup for the P06/P11 restore and RTO gates, or learns to ignore the tool.
findings.proposed_fix: After `supabase init` (line 419), when manifest.source is `linked`, copy the repository's supabase/.temp/{postgres,rest,gotrue,storage}-version and storage-migration into <scratch>/supabase/.temp/ before `supabase start`, and print the versions used.
findings.proof_recipe: In a disposable checkout write a GoTrue tag newer than the CLI default into supabase/.temp/gotrue-version, `supabase stop && supabase start` (the dev stack now runs that GoTrue and its auth schema), `pnpm backup --local`, then `pnpm restore-check <file>`. Wrong result: `The psql restore failed` with `column ... of relation ... does not exist` or `relation "auth.<table>" does not exist`.

findings.title: The real-restore runbook never deploys the Edge Functions, re-points and rebuilds the Pages site, moves the Resend webhook or applies migrations newer than the backup
findings.evidence: Steps 1-9 (lines 1334-1413) cover extract, psql restore, Vault, pg_cron, `supabase secrets set` (with the Moyasar webhook address), Auth settings, object upload, the deletion ledger and cleanup; none runs `supabase functions deploy`, although Supabase's guide lists Edge Functions as migrated separately (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/migrating-within-supabase/backup-restore). The site calls `${process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL}/functions/v1/contact` (ContactForm.tsx:107; quote.ts:318,399-400 with NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY), inlined at build. The Resend endpoint is `https://<project-ref>.supabase.co/functions/v1/resend-webhook` (operations.md:338-342); step 5 only re-sets its secret. Nothing says to link the new project and `supabase db push` migrations committed after the backup.
findings.impact: An owner restoring after losing the project ends, following the runbook line by line, with a database but no functions (contact, checkout, payments, outbox, orders all 404), a public site still calling the dead project, bounce and complaint events posted to the old address (suppression stops updating), and a schema older than the deployed code. Step 5's smoke test fails with no step explaining why, inside the RTO<=4h of VERIFICATION.md:59.
findings.proposed_fix: Add runbook steps: `supabase link --project-ref <new>` and `supabase db push` for migrations newer than the backup; `supabase functions deploy` for every function; set NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL and NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY in the Pages project and rebuild; move the Resend webhook endpoint to the new ref and store its signing secret; then the smoke test.

findings.title: The pinned package manager, pnpm 10.33.0, carries 18 published advisories (10 high), all fixed in 10.34.5; it was already vulnerable when pinned
findings.evidence: package.json:6 `"packageManager": "pnpm@10.33.0"` (set in 2cfed29, 2026-09-22; repeated in docs/development.md:12); CI installs it via pnpm/action-setup (ci.yml:33-36) and the owner's global pnpm is 10.33.0. OSV (api.osv.dev, npm pnpm 10.33.0) lists 18 advisories published 2026-06-26 to 09-02, e.g. GHSA-vq4v-j7r6-jq4m (high, fixed 10.34.5: a tarball dependency's manifest name escapes node_modules and overwrites files such as .git/hooks/pre-commit, `even with --ignore-scripts`), GHSA-5wx6-mg75-v57r (high, fixed 10.34.2: allowBuilds approval reused by a colliding locator), GHSA-c59q-g84q-2gj5 (high, lockfile depPath traversal), GHSA-rxhj-4m44-96r4 (high, malicious patch file). `npm view pnpm dist-tags`: latest-10 is 10.34.6.
findings.impact: Not reachable today: all 577 lockfile entries resolve from the registry with integrity and the one patch is ours. It becomes reachable at the next dependency update or agent-written lockfile/patch change: a compromised package pulling a crafted tarball, or a crafted lockfile entry, writes files outside node_modules during `pnpm install` on the owner's machine (where .env holds the Cloudflare token and Moyasar keys) or in CI, past the onlyBuiltDependencies policy the project relies on.
findings.proposed_fix: Set `"packageManager": "pnpm@10.34.6"` (ideally with its `+sha512.<hash>` suffix), update docs/development.md:12, and confirm `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` leaves the lockfile unchanged.

findings.title: The graft session hooks still import <repo>/dist/claude/hooks.js as a last resort and prefer the highest-versioned graft in any ancestor node_modules
findings.evidence: Line 64: `return path.join(dir, 'dist', 'claude', name); // last-ditch; import will no-op if absent`; lines 58-59 add `require.resolve('@nanonets/graft/package.json', { paths: [dir] })`, which climbs every ancestor node_modules up to C:\node_modules, and best() (46-54) keeps the highest version. `git log -- .claude/helpers/graft-hooks.cjs` lists only 8ffdb9c (baseline): AUDIT-1 G4.6, marked fixed, asked for line 64 to become `return null`; only its settings.json half was applied (c222225). settings.json runs this helper on SessionStart and Stop.
findings.impact: A committed dist/claude/hooks.js (dist/ is not ignored), or a planted C:\node_modules\@nanonets\graft with a higher version (C:\ root is writable by any local account), runs as the owner in every Claude session in this repository without a prompt.
findings.proposed_fix: Apply G4.6 as written: line 64 `return null` and import only when entry() returned a path; drop the ancestor-node_modules candidate or let BAKED win over a higher version found elsewhere.
findings.prior_overlap: AUDIT-1 G4.6 (fix holds only for settings.json)

findings.title: The backup passphrase is not Unicode-normalized before scrypt, so a visually identical Arabic passphrase can fail to open the backup
findings.evidence: Line 71 `return scryptSync(passphrase, salt, 32, SCRYPT)` hashes the string as typed; `grep -rn normalize( scripts/` finds nothing. passphrase.mjs:1-6 explicitly supports Arabic passphrases (`the same keystrokes open the backup later`) and keeps every non-control code point, combining marks and U+200C/U+200F included.
findings.impact: Arabic has canonically equivalent spellings that render identically: shadda+fatha typed in either order (U+0651 U+064E vs U+064E U+0651), أ as U+0623 or U+0627 U+0654 (an IME, a password manager or another OS that normalizes). A restore on another machine (runbook step 1: any machine) can refuse the right passphrase with WRONG_PASSPHRASE_OR_DAMAGED, and there is no reset: the backups are lost.
findings.proposed_fix: Derive from `passphrase.normalize('NFC')` in a format version 2 (version 1 keeps the raw string, or try raw then NFC when reading), and say in docs/operations.md that the passphrase is compared after NFC.

findings.title: No .gitattributes: on a Windows clone with Git's default core.autocrlf=true, check:frozen reports three frozen files as modified
findings.evidence: The repository has no .gitattributes. `git ls-files --eol deploy` shows deploy/mobile-fix.css, deploy/design/support.js and deploy/design/index.html stored i/lf; check-frozen.mjs:95-97 hashes raw working-tree bytes. This machine passes only because `git config core.autocrlf` is false; Git for Windows installs with autocrlf=true, which checks those files out as CRLF.
findings.impact: On a re-clone on another Windows machine, `pnpm check:frozen` (part of `pnpm check` and the acceptance routine) fails with `modified: deploy/...` although nothing changed; the tempting `node scripts/check-frozen.mjs --write` would record CRLF hashes and break CI on Linux.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a .gitattributes with `deploy/** -text` (byte-exact frozen sources), optionally `* text=auto eol=lf` for the rest.

findings.title: The inside-the-repository guard for --extract (and backup --out) lets through any folder whose name starts with two dots
findings.evidence: Line 70 `if (relDest === '' || (!relDest.startsWith('..') && !isAbsolute(relDest)))` refuses only paths that do not start with `..`. Measured with node: path.win32.relative('C:/repo', 'C:/repo/..plain') is `..plain`, so the guard does not block it (posix behaves the same). backup.mjs:67 uses the same test for --out.
findings.impact: `pnpm restore-check <file> --extract ..plain` from the repository root writes the decrypted dumps (auth data, TOTP secrets, every customer record) into a folder inside the repository that .gitignore does not cover, the case AUDIT-1 S17.4 meant to refuse; a later `git add -A` publishes them. Needs an unusual folder name.
findings.proposed_fix: Treat a path as outside only when `relDest === '..' || relDest.startsWith('..' + sep)` or it is absolute (sep from node:path), at restore-check.mjs:70 and backup.mjs:67.
findings.prior_overlap: AUDIT-1 S17.4 (guard added there; holds except this case)

findings.title: restore-check never checks that the scratch stack stopped, so a failed or cut-off stop leaves the restored plaintext database in a Docker volume with no message
findings.evidence: cleanup() line 401: `supabase(['stop', '--no-backup', '--workdir', scratch], { stdio: 'ignore', timeout: 300000 })`, result discarded, then rmSync(scratch). Lines 397-398 note that `supabase stop` can take minutes, longer than Windows allows after the console closes (the SIGHUP handler, line 512, only calls process.exit). The header (lines 21-22) promises the scratch stack `is stopped with --no-backup` on the way out.
findings.impact: When Docker is slow, the stop times out, or the window is closed mid-rehearsal, the scratch database volume keeps an unencrypted copy of the whole production database (auth.users, auth.mfa_factors, finance) on the owner's disk until a later rehearsal happens to clear it, and nothing tells him.
findings.proposed_fix: Check the stop result; when it is non-zero or timed out, print that the scratch stack may still hold the restored data and the command `supabase stop --no-backup --project-id anasaq-restore-check`, and exit non-zero.
