coverage:
Read in full: package.json; pnpm-lock.yaml header, importers and every resolution (577 entries, all npm registry with integrity, no git or tarball sources); .npmrc; .node-version (24.19.0, after the last Node 24 security release); .gitignore; .ignore; .git/info/exclude; .mcp.json; .claude/settings.json (and its uncommitted diff); .claude/settings.local.json; .claude/launch.json; .claude/helpers/graft-hooks.cjs and graft-statusline.cjs; .github/workflows/ci.yml line by line; eslint.config.mjs; tsconfig.json; vitest.config.ts; playwright.config.ts; next.config.ts; scripts/{backup,restore-check,check-export,check-budgets,check-copy,check-frozen,local-env,bootstrap-owner,import-content,seed-demo-catalog}.mjs; scripts/lib/{backup-format,passphrase,cron-jobs,demo-guard}.mjs; every supabase/functions/*/deno.json; artifacts/soon/{deploy.cjs,wrangler.toml,worker.js,README.md,site/_headers}; patches/page-flip@2.0.7.patch (tokenised diff: two changes that stop the requestAnimationFrame loop after destroy; it patches page-flip.browser.js, which the package's main/browser fields point at, so it reaches the app); docs/operations.md Backups (D35) and the real-restore runbook; PLANS/VERIFICATION.md; tests/unit/{backup-cli,restore-check}.test.ts. Sampled: prepare-media.mjs (process, network and sharp use), prepare-preview.py (header, imports; pypdf unpinned), tests/support/moyasar-emulator.ts (binds 127.0.0.1, local Host checks), src/lib/env.ts, src/components/book/pdf.ts, AUDIT-1 appendix and audit-result.json, AUDIT-2 report, the wave-A findings (no overlap).

Measured: pnpm audit --prod and full (saved in SCRATCH/SUPPLY); OSV for every direct dependency and for pnpm, wrangler, serve and graft; git ls-remote for the five action SHAs (all real and equal to the latest tags; permissions contents: read; no secrets; no pull_request_target; pnpm store cache is branch-scoped); the patch hash equals the lockfile hash (pnpm normalises CRLF before hashing); only esbuild and unrs-resolver declare install scripts and both are allow-listed; direct dependency licences are MIT or Apache-2.0; a full-history secret scan (values masked) found only test fakes and local 127.0.0.1 credentials; every path ever added (the ANAS_WHATSAPP_CHAT purge holds); tracked PDFs are the documented preview fragments; live anas.studio headers (CSP and noindex reach / through the ASSETS binding); `docker ps` port bindings of the running CLI stack (0.0.0.0 and [::]; read-only, no request sent to its ports); the codegraph index holds no .env or BOOK_ASSETS path.

What a green CI proves: an exact lockfile install; ESLint over app, tests, scripts and functions; tsc over all .ts/.tsx (not the .mjs scripts); 68 unit files of pure helpers; frozen deploy/ hashes; copy rules; deno check of every function entry; every migration and the seed applying from zero; the content import; the static export with 59 required files, RTL attributes, no prefix-recognisable secret and no demo text against a non-loopback origin; the public JS budget. No vacuous step was found: the deno loop fails on an empty glob or a missing deno.json under bash -eo pipefail. None of VERIFICATION.md's non-negotiable invariant tests run in CI, nor any Edge Function over HTTP, e2e, axe or restore. Branch protection on main cannot be seen from here (no credentialed GitHub call made).

Lead: lead:SUPPLY-01 confirmed and extended as SUPPLY-03. Its severity is lowered to low because nothing reaches the vulnerable code, and its line is corrected from 36 to 40. The missing CI audit step became a plan gap. No lead was refuted.

Checked and not reported:
- The Deno side floats only iceberg-js ^0.8.1 (Supabase-owned, and 0.8.1 is the only 0.8.x release), because supabase-js 2.117.1 pins its sub-packages. So `--no-lock` changes nothing today, but CI and a deploy could drift apart on a future 0.8.x.
- The backup format is sound: AES-256-GCM with the header as AAD, scrypt N=2^17 r=8 p=1, and a fresh salt and IV per file. Truncation, reordering, a swapped entry or an edited header all fail the tag. Plaintext is written before the tag is checked, but it is deleted on failure; only a killed process leaves it behind.
- The env passphrase is inherited by every supabase child process (exposed to the same user only).
- The 2.106.0 data.sql also carries pg_net's queue and response tables. A captured queue row would include the jobs bearer secret. Current pg_net sends or purges only after a wake, so a rehearsal does not replay it.
- check:export skips .mjs and .svg (one pdf worker file).
- npx-run tools are version-pinned, but their transitive trees float and npm runs their install scripts; deploy.cjs does this with the Cloudflare token in its environment.
- Next telemetry is on during builds.
- GHSA-vq4v and GHSA-5wx6 need tarball or URL dependencies, and the lockfile has none today.
- The `..` folder edge case also applies to backup --out (an encrypted file).
- Per the owner's standing order, font licences were not examined.

Not reached / next with more time:

- Check whether hosted GoTrue encrypts auth.mfa_factors secrets with a project key (a restored owner's TOTP might not verify on a new project).
- Compare the Edge Runtime's Deno version with CI's 2.9.6.

findings.title: The restore-into-a-new-project runbook never repoints the static site: the Pages build variables, the rebuild, the Resend webhook endpoint and the gate still name the old project
findings.evidence: docs/operations.md:1332-1407 (steps 1-9) restores the dumps, Vault, cron jobs, function secrets (noting 'A new project has a new <project-ref>, so FUNCTIONS_PUBLIC_URL and the webhook address in Moyasar's dashboard change with it'), Auth settings and objects, then a smoke test 'through the contact form from the site'. Nothing changes the Pages build's NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL and NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY or rebuilds: Next inlines them into every bundle and page (src/lib/media-ref.ts:123-125 builds every library image URL from it; ContactForm.tsx:107, quote.ts:318, VariantAction.tsx:57 and the admin client call it). The Resend endpoint registered at operations.md:338-340 is `https://<project-ref>.supabase.co/functions/v1/resend-webhook`, and SITE-STATE's gate reads `<SUPABASE_URL>/rest/v1/site_state` (SITE-STATE-CONTRACT.md:43); a configured Google client's redirect URI is the old project's Auth callback too.
findings.impact: Two outcomes, depending on the old project. If it is gone, nothing on the site reaches the restored project: images vanish and the contact form, cart, checkout and staff sign-in fail, and the runbook has no step that explains why. If it still answers (a restore after a bad migration or an accidental deletion, which is what a restore into a new project is for), the step-5 smoke test passes against the OLD project, so the operator believes the restore is live: the site and the admin (built with the same URL) keep creating and showing orders and messages in the old database, while the Moyasar webhook, repointed to the new project as step 5 says, delivers to a project that does not know those invoices (review payments and owner alerts there). Every order and message written after the restore exists only in the old project; repointing later or deleting the old project loses them.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a step between 5 and the smoke test: update the Pages project's NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL and NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY (production and preview), set the new `pages_deploy_hook` Vault value if the Pages project changed, trigger a build and wait for it; repoint the Resend webhook endpoint (and re-set RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET if Resend issues a new one), the Google OAuth redirect URI when Google sign-in is on, and the gate's two Supabase variables.

findings.title: A Pages build that fails after the deploy hook answered raises no signal anywhere while the owner home says «بناء الموقع: سليم»; Cloudflare's free 'Deployment failed' notification is in no plan step, and I34 records the failure as dashboard-only
findings.evidence: site_build_trigger records a run 'ok' when the hook answers 2xx (20260930140000_audit2_fixes.sql:737 `v_ok := v_answered and v_status between 200 and 299 ...`), and AdminHome renders it as «سليم» (src/components/admin/AdminHome.tsx:31). I34 (ISSUES.md:25) says 'a Pages build that breaks after the hook answered is visible only in the Pages dashboard; the owner checks it after the first publishes', and docs/operations.md:397-399 repeats it. Cloudflare's Notifications list 'Pages > Project updates' with the event 'Deployment failed', filterable by project and environment, 'Included with: All Cloudflare plans' (https://developers.cloudflare.com/notifications/notification-available/, last updated 2026-10-02). grep of PLANS/ and docs/ finds no mention of it.
findings.impact: Any later build failure (an invalid published document, a transient Supabase error or timeout during the build's fetches, a broken commit on main, the build quota) leaves the last good deploy live with no alert: a post archived for a legal reason, a corrected price or a product taken off sale stay on the public site while the owner home says the build is healthy; after a policy change and its re-approval the checkout page keeps the old revisions, so every buyer sees «نحدّث السياسات الآن؛ حاول بعد قليل.» with the button disabled (CheckoutForm.tsx:205, 782-790; src/lib/cart.ts:432-448) until a build succeeds, while the owner's screen says «الشراء مفتوح». The record frames it as a first-publishes check, but it can happen on any publish.
findings.proposed_fix: Add to P11's hosted setup (WORK-PACKAGES P11, docs/deployment.md) and to I34: create a Cloudflare notification 'Pages: Project updates' for the production environment of the Pages project with the event 'Deployment failed', delivered to the owner's email; correct I34 and docs/operations.md:397-399 to say the failure is mailed by Cloudflare and the owner home only knows the hook accepted the request (relabel the ok run, e.g. «طُلب البناء», so «سليم» is not read as 'the site is updated').
findings.prior_overlap: I34 (known open, record wrong about 'visible only in the Pages dashboard')

findings.title: ARCHITECTURE says a paused Free project is 'harmless before orders', but the launched static site needs Supabase at view time: every library image, the contact form, live availability, the cart and the notify sign-up, and every rebuild
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE.md:55: 'The hosted Free project may pause while idle; that is harmless before orders.' DECISIONS.md:87 leaves 'whether the site launches on Free before orders' to the owner (D34 launches before payments). But src/lib/media-ref.ts:123-125 bakes `${NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL}/storage/v1/object/public/media-public` into every library image (Picture.tsx renders it as ), ContactForm.tsx:107, AvailabilityForm.tsx:41, VariantAction.tsx:57 and quote.ts:318/398 call the project from the browser, and every Pages build reads it (content.ts, store.ts, journal.ts, policies.ts). Supabase: a Free project with too little 'user database activity' over 7 days is paused and must be resumed from the dashboard (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/free-project-pausing); a Free organization that continually exceeds its quota (5 GB egress + 5 GB cached, https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/manage-your-usage/egress) can be restricted by 'Pausing projects' or 'Responding with a 402 status code for all API requests' (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/billing-faq#fair-use-policy). Library images are Storage egress.
findings.impact: If the owner launches on Free, as the plan allows, a quiet week or an image-heavy traffic month takes down every image Anas uploaded through the admin (journal covers, product covers, new scenes and room pictures), the contact form, the store's live state and the cart, and stops every rebuild (the build fails and the old deploy stays), until someone resumes the project or the billing cycle resets. The plan tells him this is harmless, so the choice is made on wrong information.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace the sentence in ARCHITECTURE.md:55 and DECISIONS.md:87 with what a pause or a Fair Use restriction breaks on the launched site (the list above) and that resuming is a manual dashboard step; add to P11's launch checklist the choice 'Pro at launch, or Free with the owner watching Supabase's pause and quota mails', and list the Storage egress of library images in docs/costs.md.

findings.title: DATA-AND-SECURITY promises order lines that are 'variant or service exactly one', but finance.order_items requires a product variant, and every P08 money function keys on variant lines; P09's package lists none of them
findings.evidence: PLANS/DATA-AND-SECURITY.md:35: 'orders / order_items | ... Item variant or service exactly one'. The table: `variant_id uuid not null references public.product_variants (id), product_id uuid not null ..., sku text not null, ... fulfillment text not null check (fulfillment in ('digital', 'physical', 'signed'))` and `unique (order_id, variant_id)` (catalog_and_checkout.sql:389-402). finance.order_try_commit (payment_core.sql:617-726) locks `public.product_variants` for every line, joins `v.id = i.variant_id`, checks stock or preorder capacity, decrements stock, and creates entitlements only for fulfillment 'digital' and fulfilments only for 'physical'/'signed'; payment_attempts.order_id is NOT NULL (payment_core.sql:140), so a paid booking can only settle as an order. WORK-PACKAGES P09 Files list `_shared/{booking,calendar,checkout,email}.ts`, the bookings and calendar functions and 'finance migrations', but not payments.ts, refunds.ts, orders.ts, OrderPage, the admin order and refund views, or the commit, expiry, refund and resolution functions that would have to learn a service line.
findings.impact: P09 starts from a contract that says the line model already holds a service; the first booking round finds it cannot insert a booking line without altering a NOT NULL money table on a live database and teaching order_try_commit, apply_verified_payment's late-payment path, order_resolve, checkout_expire, the refund allocation, the receipt and the order page about it. Done inside P09's allowlist it cannot be done; done as a parallel 'booking order' it settles every paid booking as an UNMAPPED_INVOICE review (wave A DB-PAY plan gap).
findings.proposed_fix: Correct DATA-AND-SECURITY:35 to what is built, and before P09 dispatch decide the booking line shape (a nullable variant_id plus service_id/booking_id with a one-of check and a 'booking' fulfillment kind, or a booking row linked to the order) and add to P09's file list the P08 paths that must branch on it: payment_core's order_try_commit and apply_verified_payment, order_resolve, checkout_expire, the refund functions and refunds.ts, orders.ts/OrderPage.tsx, the admin order views and the receipt mail.
findings.prior_overlap: wave A DB-PAY plan gap 'P09 paid bookings must settle through the P08 payment core'; the order_items sentence dates from P07 and is not among P08-CONTRACT section 13's recorded deviations, so the planned P08-close doc update may not reach it

findings.title: Eleven of the fifteen pg_cron jobs are pure SQL, record no run and can fail every minute or every night unseen: nothing reads cron.job_run_details, and the owner home watches four jobs
findings.evidence: AdminHome's KNOWN_JOBS = ['email_outbox', 'site_build', 'media_sweep', 'backup'] (AdminHome.tsx:33). finance.job_runs is written only by public.job_run_record, which the Edge Functions call (20260926120000_contacts_and_email.sql:447-454), and by site_build_trigger (grep of `insert into finance.job_runs`); content-publish-due, checkout-expire, availability-sweep, notify-confirm-backlog, buyer-retention, contacts-purge, notifications-purge, payment-events-purge, rate-limits-purge, job-runs-purge and cron-run-details-purge run SQL directly (scripts/lib/cron-jobs.mjs listing). A failing run leaves its error only in cron.job_run_details, which no function, screen or script reads and which cron-run-details-purge deletes after 7 days (20260930140000_audit2_fixes.sql:820-823). buyer_retention_purge deletes through finance.orders_delete (20261002170000_stats_disputes.sql:78-95), which knows payment_events, payment_attempts, order_items, inventory_reservations and coupon_redemptions; any new table referencing finance.orders (P09's bookings, DATA-AND-SECURITY:41 'order optional') makes the delete raise and the whole purge roll back.
findings.impact: A job that starts failing after a migration (the likely case: P09 adds a foreign key to orders and the nightly buyer-retention purge fails every night) stops silently: D42's 90-day deletion of unpaid buyers' data, which the privacy policy is to state, simply stops; a failing checkout-expire leaves holds open, a failing availability-sweep stops restock mail, a failing publish_due stops scheduled posts. The owner home stays green and the evidence is purged after a week.
findings.proposed_fix: Add one owner/operations SQL function over cron.job_run_details (failed runs in the last 24 hours, by jobname, count and last time; no command text) and show it on the owner home as one line («مهمة مجدولة تفشل: …»); and add 'extend finance.orders_delete for every new child of finance.orders' to P09's file list.
findings.prior_overlap: wave A DB-CORE-12 (info: the contacts purge alone leaves no trace); wave A CONTRACT-02 / P08-CKPT-03 (payments_reconcile has no health line)

findings.title: P11's Pages setup line names the build command `pnpm build`, while I40 needs `pnpm build && pnpm check:export` and the Pages Next.js preset fills in `npx next build`, which skips both the demo guard and the I39 fetch-cache clear
findings.evidence: WORK-PACKAGES.md:139: 'a Cloudflare Pages project connected to the repository (build `pnpm build`, output `out` ...)'. ISSUES.md:29 (I40): 'the Pages build command must be `pnpm build && pnpm check:export` (or the deploy must gate on it) for the check to block a real deploy'. package.json:12: `build` = rmSync('.next/cache/fetch-cache') then `next build` (I39: a build reused an earlier build's responses from .next/cache/fetch-cache, artifacts/acceptance/P07/commands.txt:165-176). Cloudflare's guide for a static Next.js site sets the preset 'Next.js (Static HTML Export)' with 'Build command | npx next build' (https://developers.cloudflare.com/pages/framework-guides/nextjs/deploy-a-static-nextjs-site/), and Pages build caching restores `.next/cache` for Next.js once enabled (https://developers.cloudflare.com/pages/configuration/build-caching/).
findings.impact: An operator who follows P11 literally deploys without the demo-row check, so a hosted build that still shows «تجريبي» rows goes live; one who accepts the preset's `npx next build` also skips the fetch-cache clear, and with build caching on every later rebuild can serve the previous build's data (I39's stale catalog) while the owner home says the build succeeded.

Connected as P11 describes, every agent push becomes a public preview build against the production Supabase project, every build (preview included) counts against the 500 a month that content publishes need, and every push to main deploys to anas.studio without waiting for CI. The three deploy units are released separately: Pages builds on push, while migrations (supabase db push over DATABASE_URL, D26) and Edge Functions (supabase functions deploy) are manual CLI steps, so a push whose pages call a new RPC, column grant or function action is live before what it needs exists (the alt_ar grant note in docs/operations.md:415-419 is one instance). There is one live project and no staging (DECISIONS: one free live Supabase project).

plan_gaps.title: Rollback for a static site whose artifact carries the data: Pages rollback restores old content and the next publish silently undoes it
plan_gaps.why_needed: A Pages rollback switches production to an earlier deployment, which holds that build's data as well as its code (archived posts back, superseded policy seqs that the checkout then sends, old prices). The next publish, scheduled post or catalog change calls the deploy hook, which builds the branch head again, so the rolled-back bad code returns with no one noticing. docs/rollback.md (P11) must say: undo code by reverting the commit on main and letting the hook rebuild; use a Pages rollback only as a stopgap and expect the next publish to replace it; never roll the database back with the static site. The database side has no down path at all: supabase/migrations is forward-only, so undoing a schema change is a new forward migration or a restore (D35), and a restore into a new project also needs the site repointed (ARCH-09). The three units (migrations, functions, Pages) therefore roll back differently, and the runbook has to say in which order.
plan_gaps.touches: docs/rollback.md, docs/deployment.md (P11); PLANS/WORK-PACKAGES.md P11

findings.title: The restore runbook never enables pg_cron/pg_net before the restore, never deploys the Edge Functions, and never repoints the site, the Resend webhook and the browser at the new project
findings.evidence: "A real restore into a new hosted project" has nine steps: extract (1), psql restore (2), Vault (3), cron (4), `supabase secrets set` plus a contact-form smoke test (5), Auth settings (6), Storage upload (7), deletion ledger (8), delete the extract (9). No step runs `supabase functions deploy` (grep of docs/ for 'functions deploy' finds nothing; only PLANS/WORK-PACKAGES.md:139, a future P11 file, names it). No step changes the Pages build's NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL / NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY and rebuilds, although docs/development.md:45-47 says they are "used by the build, the browser admin and the media URLs" (a static export bakes them in). Step 5 says the new <project-ref> changes FUNCTIONS_PUBLIC_URL and the Moyasar webhook address, but not the Resend webhook endpoint `https://<project-ref>.supabase.co/functions/v1/resend-webhook` (operations.md:340). Supabase's backup/restore guide, which step 2 follows (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/migrating-within-supabase/backup-restore, fetched 2026-10-07), lists as gotchas to do before restoring: "If any non-default extensions were used in the old database, enable the Extensions" (pg_cron and pg_net here: 20260925120000_content_versions_and_publishing.sql:9, 20260927090000_static_site_and_functions.sql:23), and says Edge Functions, secrets and environment variables are not migrated. Step 2 names only the supabase_admin/cli_login_postgres caveat; scripts/restore-check.mjs:193-203 handles the extension caveat in the rehearsal, the manual runbook does not. Nor does any step say to stop the old project when it still runs (a restore after a bad data change rather than a lost project): its pg_cron, Vault secrets and function secrets keep sending mail and reconciling with the same Resend and Moyasar keys.
findings.impact: An operator restoring after losing the project ends step 5 with a database, secrets and Vault values but no functions: the smoke test's contact POST and every checkout, payment, outbox, orders, download and admin call answer 404 on the new project, and the public site and admin still call the old (lost) project's URL and key. Bounces and complaints keep going to the dead Resend endpoint, so suppression stops. The runbook gives no next step, so the shop stays down during the incident the runbook exists for.
findings.proposed_fix: Before step 2: enable pg_cron and pg_net in the new project (Database, Extensions). Before the smoke test: supabase link --project-ref <new> then supabase functions deploy (every function; per-function verify_jwt comes from supabase/config.toml); set the Pages project NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL and NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY to the new project and redeploy; edit the Resend webhook endpoint to the new project ref and set RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET to its signing secret; check that the functions can reach the database with the new project's keys (wave A EF-ADMIN-01). If the old project is still up, first pause it or delete its Vault jobs_secret and function secrets, so only one project sends mail and talks to Moyasar.
findings.prior_overlap: Related, not the same: EF-ADMIN-01 (wave A) shows a project restored or created after 2025-11-01 has no legacy service_role key, so even deployed functions fail; the restore runbook should also name that check.

findings.title: After a restore the deletion ledger is replayed only at step 8, after the mail and job secrets are live, so mail an erasure removed can go out again
findings.evidence: Steps 3-5 re-create Vault `functions_url`/`jobs_secret`, every cron job, and the function secrets including RESEND_API_KEY, then send a real contact message; step 8 ("Reapply the deletion ledger before the site reopens") comes after. privacy_buyer_erase drops a buyer's unsent mail and deletes their notification rows (20261002170000_stats_disputes.sql:777-782); privacy_erase_contacts drops pending notices (20260927140000_privacy_requests.sql:167-169). A restored older backup brings those rows back as `pending`/`confirmed`, and from step 5 `email-outbox` (every minute) and `availability-sweep` (every minute) send them.
findings.impact: A buyer or contact-form visitor who was erased after the backup was taken can receive a receipt, order-link, confirmation or availability mail, or have their contact message re-sent to staff, during the restore window, before the ledger line that erased them is re-run. That is processing of data the owner promised to delete (PDPL), on the path the ledger exists to protect.
findings.proposed_fix: Move the replay of the ledger's `privacy_erase_contacts` and `privacy_buyer_erase` lines to right after step 2 (they are SQL only and need no secret), before any Vault secret, cron schedule or function secret is set; keep the `revoke` and `privacy_erase_staff` lines where the team screen works, and say that no mail is sent until both are done.
findings.prior_overlap: none

findings.title: No secret-rotation procedure exists, and the only Vault instruction given (vault.create_secret) fails for a secret that already exists
findings.evidence: `grep -n -i rotat docs/*.md` finds no rotation procedure for any credential. The one Vault instruction is "Hosted setup (P11): `supabase secrets set JOBS_SECRET=…`, then in the SQL editor `select vault.create_secret('<the same value>', 'jobs_secret')`" (operations.md:373-375). Supabase's Vault guide (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/vault) says a secret's name is unique and changes go through `vault.update_secret('<uuid>', '<new value>', ...)`. JOBS_SECRET lives in two places that must match: the function secret checked by the `outbox` function and Vault `jobs_secret` sent by `outbox_kick()`/`payments_kick()`/`media_sweep_kick()` (20260927150000_outbox_due_since.sql:67-78, 20261002100000_payment_core.sql:1661-1672, 20260927120000_rebuild_delivery_and_media_sweep.sql:149-157). MOYASAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET must equal the Secret Token typed in Moyasar's dashboard; tokens.ts:3-4 says TOKEN_HASH_PEPPER cannot be rotated without killing every mailed link.
findings.impact: When a key leaks (Moyasar secret key, webhook secret, Resend API key or webhook secret, Turnstile secret, the jobs secret, the Pages deploy hook URL, a Supabase secret key, the analytics token) the operator has no steps: following the setup line for a new jobs secret raises a unique-name error and leaves the function and Vault values out of step, so every pg_cron kick is refused (no mail, no payment reconciliation, no media sweep) until someone notices; changing the Moyasar webhook secret on one side only makes every webhook 401 until Moyasar drops it after its last retry. A leaked deploy hook lets anyone spend the 500 Pages builds a month. Revoking the old Resend key before the new one is set exhausts every queued mail on its first attempt (wave A EF-ADMIN-18), so the order of the steps matters.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a "Rotating a secret" section to operations.md with, per secret: where it is regenerated, the exact `supabase secrets set` and `select vault.update_secret((select id from vault.secrets where name = '<name>'), '<new>')` commands, the order (for JOBS_SECRET and MOYASAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET: both sides within the same minute, then check the next job_runs row or a webhook), what breaks meanwhile, and that TOKEN_HASH_PEPPER is not rotated (a leak means re-issuing links, an owner decision). For a replaced Pages deploy hook (the same path fixes «بناء الموقع: فاشل» after five failed tries): update pages_deploy_hook with vault.update_secret, then run select public.site_build_request(); so the next minute builds without waiting for a publish.
findings.prior_overlap: none for the runbook; EF-ADMIN-18 (Resend refusal exhausts mail) and EF-ACCESS-04/EF-ACCESS-08 (pepper) are code-side neighbours

findings.title: No procedure for a webhook outage or a buyer's double-charge claim, although a second payment on a paid invoice, an unmapped payment and a dashboard refund or void reach the ledger only through the webhook
findings.evidence: A paid attempt gets `next_check_at = null` (20261002100000_payment_core.sql:1164), and `payments_kick()` wakes the job only for rows with `next_check_at <= now()` (payment_core.sql:1653-1660), so nothing re-reads a paid invoice. The runbook says only the webhook settles by payment id (payments-runbook.md:369, item 14) and that external_refund/provider_status come from "a webhook or a check" (payments-runbook.md:254). Moyasar retries a failed delivery 5 times over about 3 h 41 min, then drops it (https://docs.moyasar.com/docs/api/other/webhooks/webhook-reference.md). grep of docs for 'outage', 'twice', 'double' finds no procedure; the reconciliation screen (operations.md:947-964) lists only what the ledger already holds. The uncommitted round M1a migration keeps `next_check_at = null` on a paid attempt (20261007100000_fable_audit_payments.sql:478).
findings.impact: If the payments function is down or misconfigured longer than Moyasar's retries (a bad deploy, a webhook-secret mismatch, a paused project), a buyer's second payment on the same invoice, a payment on an unmapped invoice, or a refund or void made in Moyasar's dashboard is never recorded: no review payment, no owner alert, money held at Moyasar invisible in the admin, and a buyer who writes 'I was charged twice' meets an owner with no steps to find it until the settlement file.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a section to operations.md (after a webhook outage, or when a buyer says he paid twice): how to notice an outage (paid orders with no row in «إشعارات الدفع»; Moyasar dashboard webhook attempts); list Moyasar's payments for the window in its dashboard; for each, find the order by the invoice metadata and press «أعد الفحص» on its paid attempt (it re-reads the invoice and files a second charged payment as a review payment; it cannot see a void, EF-MONEY-09); record a dashboard refund or void with «تسجيل استرداد خارجي», which fetches the payment itself; refund a duplicate from its review payment.
findings.proof_recipe: With the emulator: pay an order (webhook on), then POST /__emulator/config {"autoWebhook":false} and POST /__emulator/pay {invoiceId, status:'paid', force:true}; wait 5 minutes and run the payments job: expect no finance.payment_reviews row and no owner_alert (the gap). Then call the admin payment-recheck on the paid attempt: expect one payment_reviews row with reason SECOND_PAYMENT (what the procedure relies on).
findings.prior_overlap: Neighbours in wave A: EF-MONEY-02 (a refused webhook leaves no trace), EF-MONEY-09 (recheck cannot see a void), P08-CKPT-03/CONTRACT-02/EF-ADMIN-20 (no health signal for the payments job). None of them asks for the operator procedure.

findings.title: The privacy data map omits several holdings and every PDPL-specific element E08 will need
findings.evidence: Not in the table: (a) the media library and the site's photos and films of identifiable people, children included (D44), with private originals kept 'as uploaded' so camera and GPS EXIF stays (docs/media-rights.md:42-46) and a free-text `rights` note (20260926090000_media_library.sql:28); (b) the seller's legal name, address and freelance-certificate number in finance.commerce_settings, snapshotted into every finance.orders.seller, with the name and the registration printed on every receipt (supabase/functions/_shared/email.ts:377-379) (only `approved_by` is listed, line 30); (c) Supabase's API gateway logs record each caller's cf-connecting-ip, x-real-ip and user-agent for every function and Data API call (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/observability/log-field-reference, "Captured HTTP headers": the API Gateway logs capture cf-connecting-ip, cf-ipcountry, user-agent, referer and x-real-ip), while the Providers row says only 'platform logs per plan' and operations.md:117 says 'no raw IP is ever stored or logged'; (d) staff IP addresses and user agents in auth.sessions, auth.audit_log_entries and auth.mfa_challenges (the auth row says 'sign-in history, sessions'). And no row or section gives a lawful basis per purpose, where each processor stores the data (the Supabase project region, Resend, Cloudflare), the deadline for answering a request, or what to do after a breach; grep of docs/ and PLANS/ for 'PDPL', 'region', 'breach' finds nothing. For copies held by providers the map tells the person to go to them ('Moyasar keeps its own payment records and Resend its sent mail, under their own policies: the person asks them', privacy-data-map.md:88), with no word on whether those providers act for Anas and so are his to handle.
findings.impact: E08 (approved privacy text, processor/location review, tested request procedure) cannot be closed from this map, and a privacy policy drafted from it would leave out children's images, the seller's own address, IP logging by the hosting provider and cross-border hosting, which are the points a Saudi PDPL review is likely to ask about.
findings.proposed_fix: Add rows (a)-(d) with purpose, readers and retention, and a short PDPL section listing for E08: the controller and contact, the lawful basis per purpose, each processor and its storage location, the request deadline, the breach procedure, the accounting retention period and how requests reach the providers that act for him. The content and its legal reading are the owner's with E08; this audit names the gaps only.

findings.title: No runbook for a paused Supabase project, although the site launches on the Free plan and the plan forbids keep-alive traffic
findings.evidence: costs.md:7 and :12: the site launches on free plans and 'Free projects are paused after 1 week of inactivity'; DECISIONS.md build policy: 'No paid Images and no fake heartbeats'. grep -n -i 'pause' docs/*.md finds only those two costs.md lines. Supabase: a Free project is inactive when it 'does not receive sufficient user database activity over the past week'; it is resumed with «Resume project» in the dashboard (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/free-project-pausing.md).
findings.impact: In a quiet week before or after launch the project pauses: the static pages still load, but the contact form, availability sign-ups, staff sign-in, scheduled publishing, the outbox and every pg_cron job stop, and the owner home cannot say so because it is down too. findings.title: No procedure for removing a staff member in a hurry when that member is an owner, for a compromised owner account, or for an owner who lost his authenticator
findings.evidence: The only removal steps are 'Revoke them in the team screen' (privacy-data-map.md:52), a privacy procedure; operations.md 'Team invites and admin function errors' covers invites only. Revoke is an owner action at aal2 with a fresh TOTP (staff-admin), and the constraint trigger staff_keep_an_owner refuses any change that leaves no active owner (20260924130000_staff_and_app_server.sql:51-75). Sign-in is a 6-digit email code (supabase/config.toml [auth.email] otp_length = 6), so whoever reads the owner's mailbox can sign in as the owner. Revoke bans but does not end sessions (wave A EF-ADMIN-02). Every step-up action needs a TOTP verified in the last five minutes: refunds, external refunds, disputes, the seller save, policy approval and the checkout switch (operations.md:925-932), and invite, role change and revoke (development.md:111-112); the only TOTP guidance is to enrol one in «الأمان» (operations.md:932), and nothing says what to do when the phone holding it is lost.
findings.impact: If the owner's mailbox or a signed-in device is taken over, or the owner leaves on bad terms, nobody has steps: with a single owner the team screen cannot revoke him at all, and with two the other owner may not know to also change the address, end the sessions and re-enrol TOTP. Meanwhile the intruder reads every buyer's name, address and phone in the orders screens and can publish content (neither needs a TOTP). An owner who loses the phone with his authenticator can no longer refund, revoke a member or close checkout until someone removes the factor outside the admin, and no document says how.

findings.title: SADAD is on by default in Moyasar test mode and appears on the hosted invoice page; its payments cannot be refunded or voided through the API, and nothing in the plan, runbook or code knows it
findings.evidence: docs.moyasar.com/docs/guides/sadad-bill/basic-integration.md (fetched 2026-10-07), line 158: 'If you use Moyasar invoices, SADAD appears on the hosted invoice page automatically when enabled. The bill's expiry matches the invoice (capped at 29 days); the invoice goes `on_hold` while awaiting payment, then `paid`.' Line 184: 'Refund, capture, and void — SADAD bills are paid out of band; calling them returns an `unsupported_operation` error.' overview.md:75: 'On by default in test; contact support to enable live.' The bill's expired_at is a date (last day to pay). Repo: runbook step 3 'Live' (payments-runbook.md:298) and 'Before live' (312-317) make no payment-method decision; contract open item 6 still asks what on_hold means (P08-CONTRACT.md:110); refunds.ts:180-182 turns any 4xx into REFUND_REFUSED; refund_record_external answers NO_DELTA unless the provider's refunded total rose; the emulator never produces on_hold or a sadadbill payment.
findings.impact: Sandbox runs (test mode, SADAD on by default): a tester who picks SADAD leaves the invoice on_hold, and a refund of that order answers «لم يتم». If SADAD is ever enabled live: a SADAD buyer can never be refunded from the admin; a bill paid later the same day (after the 20-minute hold released the stock) lands as a late payment, often paid_needs_resolution, whose only resolution (a refund) is impossible through Moyasar; an out-of-band bank refund cannot be recorded (NO_DELTA), so the order stays paid, its file stays granted and gross keeps the money.
findings.proposed_fix: Record in contract section 2: on_hold = SADAD bill awaiting payment; payment status expired = SADAD bill unpaid; SADAD refund/void unsupported. In the runbook: keep SADAD disabled on the live account unless Anas accepts manual out-of-band refunds (owner decision); add a sandbox run that picks SADAD (observe on_hold, the ~5-minute payment_paid) and keep the refund run on card payments. If SADAD is kept, add an owner action that records a refund made outside Moyasar (a succeeded refund with source 'manual') before launch.
findings.proof_recipe: Supervised sandbox run with the test key: create an invoice of at least 10000 halalas through the client, open its url, choose SADAD. Expect GET /v1/invoices/<id> to read on_hold with an initiated sadadbill payment, then payment_paid about 5 minutes later. Then POST /v1/payments/<that payment id>/refund {"amount":100}: the result that breaks the plan's refund path is 400 unsupported_operation.
findings.prior_overlap: none (wave A EF-MONEY-12 covers a failed invoice, not SADAD/on_hold)

findings.title: Visitor-triggered confirmation mail to unverified addresses shares the Resend account with receipts and sign-in codes, and Resend pauses an account whose bounce rate passes 4% or spam rate 0.08%; no brake exists and the residual counts only the quota
findings.evidence: notify_confirm_queue's only brakes are per address (1/day, 5/30 days) and 30 a day in all: `if not finance.rate_limit_take('notify-confirm:all', repeat('0', 64), 30, interval '1 day')` (notifications.sql:114); notify_subscribe accepts any syntactically valid address for an out-of-stock variant at 5 an hour per IP (:194). resend.com/docs/knowledge-base/account-quotas-and-limits.md (fetched 2026-10-07): 'All accounts must maintain a bounce rate of under 4% ... Maintaining a bounce rate above 4% may result in a temporary pause in sending' and 'spam rate of under 0.08% ... may result in a temporary pause in sending'. docs/operations.md:1189-1194 treats the abuse as quota only ('The caps protect the 100 a day'). Supabase Auth sign-in codes use the same account over SMTP (I28).
findings.impact: While any variant is sold out, someone passing Turnstile 30 times a day can sign up 30 non-existent mailboxes (random@gmail.com); each confirmation hard-bounces. At a small store's volume (tens of legitimate sends a week) the bounce rate is far above 4% within a day or two, and a single spam complaint from a person signed up by someone else exceeds 0.08% of a month's mail. A pause stops every receipt, order link, shipping and refund notice, owner alert and staff sign-in code until Resend lifts it.
findings.proposed_fix: Brake the visitor-triggered tier: in notify_confirm_queue (and outbox_claim for priority 2) skip notify_confirm while the last 7 days' notify_confirm rows with delivery bounced or complained exceed a small number (e.g. 3), queue one owner alert when it engages, and add the bounce/spam-rate rule to operations.md's residuals and the owner home's mail line. Optionally lower the 30/day cap.
findings.prior_overlap: Related wave A abuse paths DB-OPS-09 (Gmail aliases) and CLIENT-SEC-01 (sign-in codes drain the quota); neither covers Resend's bounce/spam-rate pause

findings.title: The dispute procedure only records chargebacks; Moyasar's platform terms give the merchant three business days from the information request to answer with documents, else the claim is lost with a 200 SAR fee, and 30 days to object to a statement
findings.evidence: operations.md:991-1006 and payments-runbook.md:256-265 tell the owner to record disputes by hand from Moyasar's emails and settlement files; neither says to answer them. https://moyasar.com/en/resources/platform-terms-and-conditions/ (Last revised 14 April 2026), 7.2: 'shall respond to any inquiries or requests within a period not exceeding three (3) Business Days from the date of notification'; 9.1: the 200 SAR fee applies on 'Failure to provide a response or sufficient supporting documentation within three (3) Business Days from the date of receiving the information request'; 7.6: charges 'shall be deemed correct and final if no written objection is submitted within' 30 days of the statement. artifacts/acceptance/P08/moyasar-docs-2026-10-02.md:51 recorded only the 200 SAR. The order view shows entitlements but not download use (finance.download_tokens.uses, last_used_at), the evidence a digital 'not received' claim needs.
findings.impact: An owner following the docs waits for the twice-weekly settlement file and records the chargeback; by then the three business days have usually passed, so a winnable 'not received' claim on a downloaded book is lost: the amount is deducted and 200 SAR charged each time. A payout or fee difference recorded with «تسجيل فرق» but not objected to in writing within 30 days becomes final.
findings.proposed_fix: Add to operations.md 'Disputes and payouts' and the runbook: on Moyasar's chargeback email, answer within three business days with the order's evidence (order number, items, receipt, carrier and tracking, and for a digital item the download times from finance.download_tokens via a ready SQL query), then record it; object in writing within 30 days to any statement difference before recording it. Optionally show download count and last download per entitlement in the order view.
findings.prior_overlap: none; wave A DB-OPS-12 notes the buyer export lacks download history

findings.title: Resend documents three bounce types (Permanent, Transient, Undetermined); an Undetermined bounce suppresses the address locally for good while Resend itself does not, and operations.md still says Permanent/Temporary
findings.evidence: email_event_record suppresses every bounce outside the record-only list: `and coalesce(v_bounce_type, '') not in ('temporary', 'soft', 'transient')` (audit2_fixes.sql:650). resend.com/docs/dashboard/emails/email-bounces.md (fetched 2026-10-07): 'There are three types of bounces: Permanent ... Transient ... Undetermined - where the recipient's email server bounced, but the bounce message didn't contain enough information'; email-suppressions.md: Resend suppresses on bounce only when 'the recipient's mail server permanently rejected the email'. operations.md:318-321: 'Resend documents `bounce.type` as `Permanent`/`Temporary` ... a missing or undocumented type suppresses conservatively'.
findings.impact: One unparseable bounce (an auto-responder, an odd relay) puts a buyer or staff address in finance.email_suppressions: every later receipt, shipping, refund and file-ready mail to that buyer, or every owner alert and contact notice to that staff member, is closed 'suppressed' and cannot be replayed, while Resend would still deliver. Lifting it needs hand-written SQL (EF-ADMIN-08).
findings.proposed_fix: Add 'undetermined' to the record-only list in email_event_record (a real hard bounce on the next send arrives as Permanent and suppresses then) and correct operations.md's vocabulary to Permanent / Transient / Undetermined with this rule.
findings.prior_overlap: P06 chose conservative over-suppression for undocumented types (artifacts/acceptance/P06/source-resend-bounced.md auditor note); Undetermined is now documented as not permanent. Wave A EF-ADMIN-08 covers the missing un-suppress procedure.

findings.title: An email Resend accepted and then reports as email.failed (quota, API key, domain verification) is listed as «فشل» but can never be resent: outbox_replay refuses a sent row, and a same-key resend would be answered from Resend's idempotency cache
findings.evidence: outbox_replay: `if o.status not in ('exhausted', 'uncertain') then raise exception 'Only exhausted or uncertain messages can be replayed.'` (order_emails.sql:378-379); an accepted send makes the row 'sent' and email.failed only sets delivery = 'failed' (20260930140000_audit2_fixes.sql:661-678); outbox_attention lists `o.delivery in ('bounced', 'complained', 'failed')` (order_emails.sql:422) and EmailView offers replay only for exhausted/uncertain rows (src/components/admin/EmailView.tsx:46-47). resend.com/docs/webhooks/emails/failed.md (fetched 2026-10-07): email.failed 'is triggered when there are issues such as invalid recipients, API key problems, domain verification issues, email quota limits, or other sending failures'; idempotency-keys.md: the same key within 24 hours returns 'the same response, without actually sending the email again'.
findings.impact: After a domain-verification lapse, a key problem or a quota failure Resend reports asynchronously, every affected receipt (with the buyer's order link), shipping or refund notice and owner alert stays lost: the email screen shows «فشل» with no action, operations.md gives no procedure, and DATA-AND-SECURITY's 'surface recovery in existing admin operations' is not met.
findings.proposed_fix: Let outbox_replay accept a 'sent' row whose delivery is 'failed' (not bounced, complained or suppressed): set it pending with a new idempotency key (the old one would replay Resend's cached answer), keep the suppression check, audit it, show the replay button for such rows, and add one line to operations.md.
findings.prior_overlap: Wave A EF-ADMIN-18 covers synchronous 401/403 refusals; this is the asynchronous email.failed path

findings.impact: A credit-card buyer told the money is back who sees nothing on the statement for up to two weeks writes to Anas or disputes the charge with the bank; a chargeback on an already refunded payment costs Moyasar's 200 SAR fee if lost and can return the money twice (wave A DB-POST-02).
findings.proposed_fix: Add one sentence, worded and approved by Anas, to the refund mail and the order page's refunded state: the amount goes back to the card used, usually within 3 business days for mada and up to 14 business days for other cards.
findings.prior_overlap: Wave A DB-POST-02 (chargeback after refund) is the consequence path

findings.title: The Svix verifier is tested only against the test file's own re-implementation of the signing scheme; it does match Svix's published vector, but no test pins that
findings.evidence: The test signs with `createHmac('sha256', key).update(`${svixId}.${timestamp}.${rawBody}`).digest('base64')` (resend-webhook.test.ts:46-51), the same reading of the scheme the verifier implements (email.ts:651-665), so a shared misreading would pass both. A read-only scratch script ran the repository's verifySvixSignature against Svix's published example (https://docs.svix.com/receiving/verifying-payloads/how-manual: secret whsec_plJ3nmyCDGBKInavdOK15jsl, msg_loFOjxBNrRLzqYUf, timestamp 1731705121, signature v1,rAvfW3dJ/X/qxhsaXPOyyCGmRKsaKWcsNccKXlIktD0=): accepted; a changed body and a timestamp 6 minutes old were refused.
findings.impact: None today. A later change to the verifier or to the helper could drift from Svix's real scheme without a test failing, and every Resend event (bounces, complaints) would then be refused with 401 until Resend disables the endpoint.
findings.proposed_fix: Add one unit case with Svix's published vector (secret, id, timestamp, body, signature as on the page; now fixed to the timestamp) expecting true.
findings.prior_overlap: none

The plan has no step that chooses the methods and no way to record an out-of-band refund (VENDOR-PAY-01).

plan_gaps.why_needed: Moyasar's terms give three business days from the information request to answer with documents, else the claim is lost with a 200 SAR fee, and 30 days to object to a statement (VENDOR-PAY-07); the order view does not show download use (finance.download_tokens).

plan_gaps.why_needed: A pause of the shared Resend account stops receipts and staff sign-in codes (VENDOR-PAY-02); nothing monitors the rates, and buyers' typo'd addresses alone can push a small store's bounce rate past 4%.

findings.title: The owner's visit statistics ask Cloudflare for 7 days in one httpRequestsAdaptiveGroups query, but the dataset caps each query's time range by plan (a Free zone is reported at 1 day), and nothing checks or splits it
findings.evidence: analytics.ts:37 `const WINDOW_DAYS = 7`; analyticsWindow() builds one [now-7d, now) range used by both VISITS_QUERY and TOP_PATHS_QUERY (lines 75-105, 108-113); any GraphQL `errors` entry returns {status:'unavailable', reason:'GRAPHQL_ERROR'} (lines 258-260). Cloudflare: 'Each data node has its limits, such as ... the maximum time period (in seconds) that can be requested in one query' and 'Node limits are tied to requested zoneTag ... Higher plans ... can query over broader historical intervals' (https://developers.cloudflare.com/analytics/graphql-api/limits/, updated Oct 2, 2026); the per-zone value is the settings node's `maxDuration` (https://developers.cloudflare.com/analytics/graphql-api/features/discovery/settings/; its sample shows 259200 s = 3 days for an adaptive node). A third-party integration tested against standard zones reports httpRequestsAdaptiveGroups 'rejects any query window wider than 1 day ... cannot request a time range wider than 1d, but your query time range spans 1w' (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/urdigitalau/mcp-integrations/main/packages/cloudflare/README.md). docs/operations.md:518-523 tells the operator to confirm only edgeResponseContentTypeName and maxPageSize at E11, not maxDuration.
findings.impact: On the anas.studio zone (Cloudflare Free, docs/costs.md) every stats refresh can answer a GraphQL time-range error, so «الزيارات» and «أكثر الصفحات طلبًا» on /admin/stats show «غير متاح: ردّ الإحصاءات يحتوي على خطأ.» for ever. The owner never gets the traffic numbers the stats screen (P06) was built for, and E11's checklist would not tell him why. Fails safe (no invented numbers): data is absent, not wrong.
findings.proposed_fix: Read `settings { httpRequestsAdaptiveGroups { maxDuration notOlderThan maxPageSize } }` once per isolate (or at E11 and record it), and when maxDuration is below 7 days split the window into maxDuration-sized slices: sum `sum.visits` across slices and merge top-path counts by path before filtering and taking the top 10 (7 one-day slices = 14 queries per 5-minute cache, far inside 300 queries per 5 minutes). Add maxDuration to the E11 check in docs/operations.md:518-523 and PLANS/ARCHITECTURE.md:105.
findings.proof_recipe: With the E11 least-privilege token on the anas.studio zone: POST https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/graphql {query: 'query($z:string){viewer{zones(filter:{zoneTag:$z}){settings{httpRequestsAdaptiveGroups{enabled maxDuration notOlderThan maxPageSize}}}}}', variables:{z:<zone id>}}. Wrong result: maxDuration below 604800. Then run VISITS_QUERY from analytics.ts with a 7-day range: wrong result is an errors[] entry such as 'cannot request a time range wider than 1d', and the admin stats action answering visits unavailable GRAPHQL_ERROR.
findings.prior_overlap: none: AUDIT-1/AUDIT-2 and operations.md cover maxPageSize, the content-type filter and sampling, not the per-query time range

findings.title: The 18 room films are served from the Pages origin, which answers Range requests with 200 and the whole file; Safari on iPhone and Mac needs 206 to play MP4, so the films are likely to fail on Apple devices
findings.evidence: VideoTile.tsx:97 `<source src={`/${entry.file}`} type="video/mp4" />`: every film (/started, /built, /passed; public/media/*.mp4, up to 11.4 MB, I33) is a same-origin static file, so at launch Cloudflare Pages serves it. Cloudflare Pages (https://developers.cloudflare.com/pages/configuration/serving-pages/, updated Apr 21, 2026): 'Pages currently returns 200 responses for HTTP range requests; however, the team is working on adding spec-compliant 206 partial responses.' Live check 2026-10-07 on the owner's own Pages project: `curl -H 'Range: bytes=100-199' https://anas-v2-ansaq.pages.dev/uploads/anas-portrait.jpg` -> `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`, `Content-Length: 318857`, no Content-Range or Accept-Ranges. Apple (Safari Web Content Guide, 'Configuring Your Server'): 'HTTP servers hosting media files for iOS must support byte-range requests, which iOS uses to perform random access in media playback.' Cloudflare (https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/troubleshooting/mp4-videos-on-ios-and-safari/, May 4, 2026): 'Safari on macOS and iOS devices may fail to load MP4 video files ... Safari and iOS devices rely on HTTP range requests'; its fix forwards ranges to an origin that honours them, which Pages does not. ISSUES.md I33 offers committing the films to Pages ('each is under Pages' 25 MiB file limit') as one of two options; local runs serve ranges and Playwright's WebKit does not use Apple's media stack, so no suite would notice.
findings.impact: An iPhone or Mac Safari visitor (a large share of Saudi visitors) taps «تشغيل» on any of Anas's films and gets «تعذّر تشغيل المقطع. حاول مرة أخرى.» or a black frame, on three of the eight rooms, from launch day. Seeking and resuming also break where playback starts at all.
findings.proposed_fix: Decide I33 for a host that answers Range with 206 before P10's hosted preview: a public R2 bucket on a media subdomain (range support, no egress fee) or the Supabase Storage public bucket (its renderer sets Accept-Ranges and Content-Range, but each play counts against the 5 GB Free egress), and point public/media/manifest.json `file` at it. Add to I32/P10: on the preview, `curl -H 'Range: bytes=0-1'` a film URL must answer 206, and one film must play on a real iPhone.
findings.proof_recipe: Deploy the export to a Pages preview with the films committed. `curl -sI -H 'Range: bytes=0-1' https://<preview>.pages.dev/media/raha-drone-opening_landscape.mp4`: wrong result is 200 with the full Content-Length and no Content-Range. Then open /built in Safari on an iPhone and tap «تشغيل» on the drone film: wrong result is the failure status or a frame that never starts.
findings.prior_overlap: I33 (where the films live) is open but does not consider range support; I32's file-reply Range check covers only the paid file on Storage

findings.title: The runbook's restore into a new hosted project never redeploys the Edge Functions or rebuilds the site against the new project, so its own contact-form smoke test fails, or passes against the old project
findings.evidence: docs/operations.md:1332-1408, 'A real restore into a new hosted project', steps 1-9: extract, create the project and psql-restore, Vault, pg_cron, `supabase secrets set`, Auth settings, Storage objects, deletion ledger, cleanup. No step runs `supabase functions deploy` against the new project, changes the Pages build variables or rebuilds the site, or re-registers the Resend webhook endpoint. Supabase's own guide for moving to a new project has a separate 'Migrating edge functions' section ending in `supabase functions deploy --project-ref your_target_project_ref` (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/migrating-within-supabase/backup-restore.md, fetched 2026-10-07). A new project has a new ref and new API keys, and the static export inlines the old ones at build time: ContactForm.tsx:107 `fetch(`${process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL}/functions/v1/contact``, likewise AvailabilityForm.tsx:41, quote.ts:318, orders.ts:102, the admin client (src/lib/supabase/browser.ts:13-14) and every library image (media-ref.ts:15-16, the old project's Storage host). Step 5 ends: 'finish with a smoke test: send one real message through the contact form from the site. It must answer «received» (201)'.
findings.impact: After a disaster restore the owner follows the runbook and then: if the old project is gone, the site's forms, admin sign-in and every library image fail and the runbook gives no next step; if the old project still exists (restoring after corruption or a bad migration), the smoke test succeeds against the OLD project, so the owner declares the restore done while contact messages, sign-ups, orders and staff sign-ins keep going to the abandoned database. The new project has no functions, so its pg_cron jobs (step 4) call 404s and nothing is mailed or reconciled.
findings.proposed_fix: Add the missing steps before the smoke test: `supabase link --project-ref <new>` then `supabase functions deploy` (all nine, with config.toml's verify_jwt settings); set the Pages project's NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL and NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY to the new project and run a production build (and, once SITE-STATE-1 exists, the gate's two variables); re-point the Resend webhook endpoint to the new functions URL (new RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET) and Google's OAuth redirect URI if Google sign-in is on. Make the smoke test confirm the request goes to the new ref.
findings.prior_overlap: same wave, found independently: ARCH-09, SUPPLY-07, OPS-PRIVACY-01 (restore runbook); wave A EF-ADMIN-01 (a restored project has no legacy keys)

findings.title: The plan treats verify_jwt = true as a gateway JWT check for admin and staff-admin, but Supabase's gateway now lets any publishable key through, so it authenticates nobody
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE.md:95 'Public functions set verify_jwt = false ... the rest require a Supabase JWT at the gateway and check the role again.'; supabase/config.toml:447-453 pins verify_jwt = true on admin and staff-admin 'so a future default change ... must not silently expose the staff endpoints'. Supabase (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/functions/auth-headers.md, fetched 2026-10-07): 'For migration compatibility, verify_jwt accepts publishable and secret keys on either header, so a key on apikey passes the check too. The check alone doesn't authenticate a caller that sends only an API key.' The publishable key is in every page of the export. Today both handlers verify the caller themselves before reading the body: admin.ts:184-193 (staffFromRequest, then request.text()) and staff-admin/index.ts:44-59.
findings.impact: No exposure today, because the in-function getClaims check is the real gate. The risk is the next staff-only function (P09 calendar management, P12 board move, any new admin action) written on the plan's word that the gateway already demands a staff JWT: with only verify_jwt = true and no in-code check, anyone holding the public key reaches it. Every anonymous call to admin or staff-admin is also a billed invocation (wave A EF-ACCESS-14 assumed these two were gateway-protected).
findings.proposed_fix: Change ARCHITECTURE.md:95 and the config.toml:447-448 comment to say the gateway check admits the public key and is not authentication; every staff function must call staffFromRequest (or @supabase/server with auth: 'user') before any other work, and the P09/P12 contracts should repeat that rule.
findings.prior_overlap: none; wave A EF-ACCESS-14 and EF-ADMIN-03 assumed a genuine JWT was needed to reach admin

findings.title: secure_password_change is described as closing the password-change path, but Supabase Auth lets any session younger than 24 hours set a password without reauthentication; only the access-token hook stops password sign-in
findings.evidence: config.toml:234-236 '# Staff have no passwords (D08); the hook below refuses password sign-in, this closes the change path too.' / 'secure_password_change = true'; ARCHITECTURE.md:18 and DATA-AND-SECURITY.md:99 list it beside the hook as the enforcement; ISSUES.md I28 makes it a hosted step. GoTrue (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/supabase/auth/master/internal/api/user.go lines 153-165): 'if config.Security.UpdatePasswordRequireReauthentication { ... if session == nil || now.After(session.CreatedAt.Add(24*time.Hour)) { if len(params.Nonce) == 0 { ... ReauthenticationNeeded': a session created in the last 24 hours sets a password with no nonce, and an older one only needs the reauthentication code mailed to the staff inbox.
findings.impact: Any staff session (or a stolen one) can add a password to its account at once. It cannot be used to sign in while the Custom Access Token hook answers 403, so nothing is exposed today; but the hook is a hosted dashboard setting (I28), and if it is ever off or mis-wired on the hosted project the password works, while the plan believes a second layer exists.
findings.proposed_fix: Reword config.toml:235, ARCHITECTURE.md:18 and DATA-AND-SECURITY.md:99 to say the hook is the only control (secure_password_change only adds a reauthentication step for sessions older than 24 hours), and keep I28's password-grant 403 check as the acceptance proof of the hook on the hosted project.
findings.prior_overlap: AUDIT-1 S01.4 introduced the hook and the setting; no earlier audit checked the 24-hour rule

findings.title: config.toml leaves auto_expose_new_tables unset and documents unset as 'not auto-exposed, removed on 2026-10-30'; Supabase CLI 2.116.0 made unset mean auto-expose and dropped that date, so any CLI upgrade silently changes the local grants
findings.evidence: config.toml:19-24: '# When unset, new entities are NOT auto-exposed, matching the new cloud default. ... deprecated and the field is removed on 2026-10-30 ...' / '# auto_expose_new_tables = true'. True for the pinned CLI 2.106.0 (release notes 2026-06-11: 'auto_expose_new_tables now resolves to false when unset'; local start/reset revoke default privileges on new public tables, sequences and functions). Supabase CLI PR #6337 (https://github.com/supabase/cli/pull/6337), merged 2026-08-26, released in v2.116.0 ('auto_expose_new_tables defaults to true'): 'The 2026-05-30 flip ... anticipating a cloud default change that never landed — platform projects still auto-expose new entities ... unset ≡ explicit true ... The deprecation warning and the 2026-10-30 removal narrative are removed'. The current CLI is v2.120.0 (2026-10-06); .github/workflows/ci.yml:82 pins 2.106.0; Supabase's changelog post 45329 still announces enforcement on all existing projects on 2026-10-30.
findings.impact: The day the CLI is bumped (CI pin or a developer's machine), `supabase start`/`db reset` stop revoking postgres's default privileges for service_role, so the local stack grants service_role full access to every new public table while the hosted project, if the 2026-10-30 enforcement lands, grants none. A later migration that forgets an explicit service_role grant then passes every local and CI test and fails on the hosted project with 42501. anon and authenticated are not affected (20260924130000 revokes their defaults itself). The comment also gives an operator a removal date the CLI has withdrawn.
findings.proposed_fix: Set `auto_expose_new_tables = false` explicitly under [api] in supabase/config.toml (the behaviour every current test already runs on) and rewrite the comment to say the platform default and its date are contested; add to I28 a hosted check of `pg_default_acl` for schema public after the migrations.
findings.prior_overlap: wave A DB-CORE-05 (service_role default table privileges on hosted) is the other side of the same default

findings.title: next 16.3.5 is inside a critical advisory's range (GHSA-vcvr-r3jv-pc5j, next/og ImageResponse RCE, fixed in 16.3.6); not reachable here, but P10's 'no silently suppressed critical' gate will stop on it
findings.evidence: package.json:40 `"next": "16.3.5"` (eslint-config-next 16.3.5 at line 55). GitHub Advisory Database (https://api.github.com/advisories?ecosystem=npm&affects=next, fetched 2026-10-07): GHSA-vcvr-r3jv-pc5j, published 2026-09-30, critical, 'Remote Code Execution in next/og ImageResponse', vulnerable '>= 16.2.0, < 16.3.6'. It needs attacker-controlled values in the Node ImageResponse's SVG; `grep -rn 'next/og|ImageResponse|opengraph-image' src` finds nothing and a static export renders at build time only, so the site is not exploitable. npm has 16.3.6-16.3.8 and 16.4.0 since. PLANS/VERIFICATION.md:57: 'No silently suppressed critical/high runtime vulnerability.' pdfjs-dist 6.3.289 is outside GHSA-hq66-cqwq-w95j (fixed 6.2.108); @supabase/supabase-js 2.117.1 has no advisory.

findings.title: The P10 CSP specification lists script-src for Turnstile but not the frame-src Turnstile requires, and no img-src for the Supabase Storage host that serves every library image
findings.evidence: DATA-AND-SECURITY.md:101 defines P10's full CSP as `style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'`, `script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://challenges.cloudflare.com` without unsafe-eval, `worker-src 'self'`, `connect-src` for the Supabase Data API and /functions/v1, and the Web Analytics hosts if enabled; VERIFICATION.md:45 repeats it as the P10 gate. Cloudflare (https://developers.cloudflare.com/turnstile/reference/content-security-policy/, May 5, 2026): 'you must configure it to allow Turnstile's scripts and iframes ... script-src: https://challenges.cloudflare.com / frame-src: https://challenges.cloudflare.com'. Library images come from `${NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL}/storage/v1/object/public/media-public` (src/lib/media-ref.ts:15-16), another origin. Local runs cannot catch either: next dev does not apply public/_headers, and several specs stub the Turnstile script (docs/development.md:369-376).
findings.impact: If P10 writes the listed directives under a restrictive default-src (the usual base), the Turnstile iframe is blocked on /contact, the availability sign-up, order-link recovery and checkout, so every public form fails closed, and every library image (journal covers, product photos) is blocked. Only the hosted-preview check would show it, after the headers ship.
findings.proposed_fix: Amend the CSP list in DATA-AND-SECURITY.md:101 and VERIFICATION.md:45 with `frame-src https://challenges.cloudflare.com`, `img-src 'self' data: <the Supabase project origin>` (plus `media-src` for the films' host if I33 moves them), `font-src 'self'` and `connect-src 'self'` beside the Supabase origins; keep the hosted-preview check.
findings.prior_overlap: same wave: ARCH-06 (the same CSP omissions); I46 assigns the full CSP to P10; wave A CLIENT-SEC-05 covers HSTS/COOP

plan_gaps.title: Record the Cloudflare Pages versus Workers Static Assets decision before P11 builds the hosting
plan_gaps.why_needed: D32 and P11 put the static export on a new Cloudflare Pages project. Cloudflare now says 'Workers Static Assets is the recommended way to deploy static sites ... If you are starting a new project, use Workers instead of Pages. Pages continues to work, but new features and optimizations are focused on Workers' (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/best-practices/workers-best-practices/; migration guide updated Sep 22, 2026). The choice changes P11: the SITE-STATE gate is native on Workers (run_worker_first patterns on the same Worker, instead of a Worker route or a Pages _middleware whose responses _headers do not reach); the soon Worker anas-studio-soon already is a Workers Static Assets project on the domain, so no custom-domain move (a Worker Custom Domain cannot coexist with the CNAME a Pages custom domain creates, and Pages warns of errors until a re-pointed domain is active); Workers Builds deploy hooks (since 2026-04-01) deduplicate bursts and are limited to 10/min, while every Pages deploy-hook POST builds against 500 builds a month; Workers Builds Free is metered in build minutes (3,000/month). Either way the hook URL in Vault, _headers, 404 handling (explicit not_found_handling on Workers) and film range support (VENDOR-PLAT-04) must be re-checked on the chosen platform.
plan_gaps.touches: PLANS/DECISIONS.md (a D-entry amending D32's hosting line), PLANS/WORK-PACKAGES.md P11, PLANS/SITE-STATE-CONTRACT.md 'What P11 decides', docs/costs.md, artifacts/soon/{wrangler.toml,README.md}

plan_gaps.title: Add a hosted check that verify_jwt = true on admin and staff-admin accepts the project's current JWT signing key
plan_gaps.why_needed: Supabase's docs disagree: https://supabase.com/docs/guides/functions/auth-headers.md says the platform check validates HS256 and asymmetric signing-key JWTs, while https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/signing-keys.md says rotating to the new signing keys 'might break your app' for functions with Verify JWT and 'You will need to turn off this setting'. A gateway 401 on admin and staff-admin would stop media uploads, stats, refunds, disputes, commerce settings and the team screen. Neither I28 nor I32 lists it.
plan_gaps.touches: PLANS/ISSUES.md I28 or I32; supabase/config.toml:447-453 if it fails (verify_jwt = false is safe there because both handlers verify the caller first, VENDOR-PLAT-02)

plan_gaps.title: Say what a Free-plan pause does to the launched site, and either start on Pro or give the owner the resume procedure
plan_gaps.why_needed: D34 lets the site launch before payments and DECISIONS leaves 'whether the site launches on Free before orders' to the owner, but ARCHITECTURE.md:55 calls the pause 'harmless before orders' and no runbook mentions it. A Free project with low activity over 7 days is paused after a warning email (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/free-project-pausing.md); the static pages stay up, but every library image (served from the project's Storage host), the contact form, availability sign-ups, the admin and staff sign-in, scheduled publishing and rebuilds stop until someone presses Resume; the SITE-STATE gate falls back to MODE. Static page views do not query the database, so a quiet week can trigger it. Free also keeps Auth logs 1 hour and platform logs 1 day (https://supabase.com/pricing). Same wave: ARCH-02, OPS-PRIVACY-09 and the PLAN-GAPS slice raise the same question.
plan_gaps.touches: PLANS/ARCHITECTURE.md:55, docs/operations.md ('The owner's routine'), PLANS/DECISIONS.md (Free-or-Pro launch choice), docs/costs.md

doc_claims_checked.claim: Supabase Free projects pause after low activity over 7 days, with a warning email first, and can be restored for up to 1 year
doc_claims_checked.evidence: https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/free-project-pausing.md: 'low activity over a 7-day period'; 'A warning email roughly one week before'; 'restore a paused project for up to 1 year'.

doc_claims_checked.claim: Supabase Free has no automatic backups; Pro keeps 7 days; PITR ~$100/month per 7 days and needs Small compute
doc_claims_checked.evidence: https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/backups.md: backups for 'Pro, Team, and Enterprise'; Pro 'last 7 days'; PITR 7 days '~$100'; 'at least a Small compute add-on'; 'Database backups do not include objects you store via the Storage API' (D35's backup covers Storage).

doc_claims_checked.evidence: https://supabase.com/docs/guides/functions/limits.md: 256MB; Free 150s; paid 400s; CPU 2s; request idle timeout 150s.

doc_claims_checked.evidence: https://supabase.com/docs/guides/storage/uploads/file-limits.md: Free limit 'can't exceed 50 MB'; a bucket limit cannot exceed the global one (paid-files bucket is 100 MiB).

doc_claims_checked.evidence: https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/rate-limits.md: MFA challenge/verify, IP, not customizable, '15 requests per minute, with bursts up to 30'.

doc_claims_checked.evidence: https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/auth-mfa.md: aal claim; '$.amr[0] ... the most recent'. hasRecentTotp scans the whole array.

doc_claims_checked.claim: The Custom Access Token hook runs before every token issue; authentication_method 'password' identifies a password grant; an error object refuses it
doc_claims_checked.evidence: https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/auth-hooks/custom-access-token-hook.md and https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/auth-hooks.md (error with http_code; available on Free; Postgres hooks 2 s).

doc_claims_checked.claim: auto_expose_new_tables unset = not exposed; flag removed on 2026-10-30
doc_claims_checked.evidence: Contested: changelog 45329 (https://supabase.com/changelog/45329-breaking-change-tables-not-exposed-to-data-and-graphql-api-automatically.md) announces enforcement on all projects 2026-10-30; CLI PR #6337 (v2.116.0) says the cloud change 'never landed', makes unset = true and drops the date. No effect on what these migrations' code can reach (anon/authenticated defaults revoked by 20260924130000; service_role granted explicitly where tables are touched). See VENDOR-PLAT-05.

doc_claims_checked.claim: verify_jwt = true makes the gateway require a Supabase JWT
doc_claims_checked.evidence: https://supabase.com/docs/guides/functions/auth-headers.md: verify_jwt 'accepts publishable and secret keys on either header ... The check alone doesn't authenticate a caller'. VENDOR-PLAT-02.

doc_claims_checked.claim: verify_jwt keeps working whatever JWT signing key the hosted project uses
doc_claims_checked.evidence: auth-headers.md says HS256 and asymmetric JWTs are validated; https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/signing-keys.md says rotation 'might break your app' for Verify JWT functions. Hosted test: call admin {action:'status'} with an owner session after checking the current signing key; wrong result is a gateway 401.

doc_claims_checked.evidence: https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/extensions/pg_net.md: requests start after commit; responses stored 6 hours; unlogged tables; default timeout 2000 ms (the migrations' '5 s default' comment is stale; code passes 15000).
